Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Solvency and Financial Condition Report production chain and its internal control matrix end to end; escalates control failures to the CFO and the Audit Committee before the SFCR is approved

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Reporting Part (SFCR) read together with PS3/24 'Review of Solvency II: Reporting and disclosure phase 2' (two-part SFCR: Part 1 policyholder-facing, Part 2 other stakeholders, applying from the 31 December 2024 reference date), plus Conditions Governing Business 4-6 and Solvency Capital Requirement – General Provisions 3; re-read at each year-end SFCR kick-off and after every PRA policy statement touching Reporting or Valuation

In-scope processes.value: The UK SFCR production chain only: Solvency UK balance sheet build → technical provisions handoff from the actuarial function → own funds classification and tiering → SCR/MCR assembly → Sections A-E narrative drafting → external audit of the relevant elements → board approval → PRA submission and public website publication

In-scope systems.value: UK statutory GL plus the Solvency UK valuation overlay that feeds template S.02.01 (balance sheet); technical provisions arrive from the actuarial modelling platform and the assembled SFCR is version-controlled in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: SFCR Production and Control Manual — RACI per SFCR Section A (Business and performance), B (System of governance), C (Risk profile), D (Valuation for solvency purposes), E (Capital management); the 42-line ICFR control matrix covering data, valuation, disclosure and IT general controls; and the PS3/24 Part 1 / Part 2 template map

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and noted by the Audit Committee at its Q4 sitting; refreshed annually before the year-end kick-off and on any PRA policy statement or Dear CFO letter affecting SFCR content

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual only: the SFCR must be published and submitted to the PRA within 14 weeks of the 31 December reference date for a solo UK insurer (20 weeks at group level). Internal hard gates back-scheduled at week 6 (solvency balance sheet lock), week 9 (audit of relevant elements complete), week 12 (board approval)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every matrix control is a dated task in the close calendar with alerts at T-10 and T-3 business days to the named control owner; a gate missed by one day auto-escalates daily to the Controller and weekly to the CFO

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed control matrix, per-control preparer/reviewer evidence, GL-to-S.02.01 reconciliations, the auditor's report on the relevant elements and the approved SFCR retained 10 years from publication date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each failed, late or unevidenced SFCR control is raised as a control deficiency rated deficiency / significant deficiency / material weakness, with root cause, remediation owner and a re-test date before the next reference date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off remediation of any significant deficiency touching the solvency balance sheet, own funds tiering or the SCR before the SFCR is put to the board

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All 42 controls in the SFCR control matrix for the 31 December reference date, plus every data feed line the matrix claims to cover in templates S.02.01 (balance sheet), S.12.01 (life technical provisions), S.23.01 (own funds) and S.25.01 (SCR standard formula)

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A control fails if its evidence is missing, undated, unsigned, or performed after its reporting gate. Any failure over the solvency balance sheet, own funds tiering or the SCR is automatically rated a significant deficiency; one or more significant deficiencies blocks board sign-off of the SFCR until remediated or disclosed

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The control operates continuously but produces one annual SFCR, so testing runs twice: a design walkthrough on Q3 data in October and a full operating-effectiveness test across the year-end run in February-March

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit performs and signs the testing; no tester may own, perform or review any control in the SFCR matrix

Evidence location for test results.value: SFCR ICFR test file (matrix version, walkthrough notes, sampled evidence, deficiency log, conclusion memo) held in AuditBoard and cross-referenced from the compliance evidence repository under the reference date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Control matrix, deficiency log, GL-to-S.02.01 reconciliation and conclusion memo producible for a PRA supervisory review or the external auditor's SFCR relevant-elements audit within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager routes PRA questions through the firm's named supervisory contact; the CFO clears any statement acknowledging a control weakness, and material weaknesses are notified under Fundamental Rule 7 before the SFCR is published

checklist.step: Open the year-end SFCR cycle and re-scope the control matrix
actions: Copy last year's SFCR control matrix into a new version folder named SFCR-<reference year> in the financial reporting repository.
List every change since the last reference date that alters the chain: new PRA rules from PS3/24, new products, a new reinsurance treaty, a ledger migration, an outsourced valuation.
For each change, add, retire or amend matrix rows and record the reason in the change column so the version history explains itself.
Send the redlined matrix to the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Appointed Actuary for challenge, and record their replies.
checklist.done: the matrix version for the reference year exists, every change is reasoned, and both the reporting and actuarial owners have replied in writing.

checklist.step: Map every PS3/24 SFCR section and template to a named control owner
actions: Build a two-column map: SFCR Part 1 (policyholder-facing summary) and Part 2 (Sections A-E plus the annexed quantitative templates) against the matrix rows that assure each one.
Name one accountable owner and one reviewer per row — no row may carry a team name instead of a person.
Flag any section with no supporting control (typically Section C risk profile narrative and Section B outsourcing disclosure) and raise a matrix gap.
Circulate the map to owners with the close calendar dates attached and collect acceptance by email.
checklist.done: every SFCR section and annexed template has a named owner, a named reviewer and at least one matrix control, with acceptances on file.

checklist.step: Lock the balance sheet feeds and reconcile the GL to template S.02.01
actions: After the UK GAAP/IFRS ledger close, export the trial balance at the 31 December reference date by legal entity and reporting currency.

Run the Solvency UK valuation overlay and produce the bridge from statutory carrying value to Solvency UK fair value line by line (investments, reinsurance recoverables, deferred tax, intangibles written to nil).
Reconcile every S.02.01 asset and liability row to the bridge and investigate any difference above the £250k posting tolerance with the owning accountant before the week-6 lock.
Freeze the ledger period, record the freeze timestamp, and attach the signed reconciliation to matrix row BS-01.
checklist.done: S.02.01 ties to the frozen trial balance through a signed bridge with no unexplained difference above tolerance.

checklist.step: Control the technical provisions handoff from the actuarial function
actions: Receive from the actuarial function the signed technical provisions pack: best estimate liability, risk margin at the reformed 4% cost-of-capital rate with the tapering factor, matching adjustment benefit and any transitional measure on technical provisions.
Check the model run identifier and valuation date on the pack match the run registered in the model governance repository — reject any pack quoting an unregistered run.
Tie the pack totals into S.12.01 (life) row by homogeneous risk group and into S.02.01 technical provisions, and record the tie-out in the handoff control sheet.
Have the Appointed Actuary countersign the handoff sheet before the numbers enter the reporting chain.
checklist.done: the technical provisions in S.12.01 and S.02.01 trace to one registered model run on a countersigned handoff sheet.

checklist.step: Control own funds classification, tiering and the EPIFP disclosure
actions: Build the S.23.01 own funds schedule: reconciliation reserve, ordinary share capital, subordinated liabilities, and each instrument's tier under the Own Funds Part.

For every subordinated instrument, re-read the terms sheet against the tiering conditions (permanence, subordination, absence of incentives to redeem) and record the tier conclusion with the clause reference.

Calculate expected profits included in future premiums (EPIFP) using the prescribed method — value the best estimate with future premiums set to nil and take the difference — and post the result to S.23.01 row R0790.
Apply the tiering eligibility limits against the SCR and MCR and show the restricted amounts explicitly.
Route the schedule to the Head of Capital Management for review sign-off.
checklist.done: own funds are tiered instrument by instrument with clause references, the EPIFP figure is computed on the prescribed basis and sits in R0790, and eligibility limits are applied.

checklist.step: Control the SCR and MCR assembly into S.25.01 and S.28
actions: Assemble the standard formula modules — market, counterparty default, life underwriting, health, non-life, intangible — and apply the prescribed correlation matrices to derive the Basic SCR.
Add the operational risk charge and deduct the loss-absorbing capacity of technical provisions and deferred taxes, documenting the LACDT justification against the deferred tax recognised in S.02.01.
Populate S.25.01 module by module and compute the MCR in S.28 with the linear formula plus the floor and cap against the SCR.
Reconcile the SCR coverage ratio in the SFCR narrative to the eligible own funds from S.23.01 — the ratio quoted in Section E must be recomputable from the annexed templates.
Attach the module workbook and the correlation evidence to matrix row SCR-03.
checklist.done: S.25.01 and S.28 are populated, the LACDT deduction is justified, and the Section E coverage ratio recomputes from the annexed templates.

checklist.step: Evidence IT general controls over the reporting chain
actions: List every system in the chain — ledger, valuation overlay, actuarial modelling platform, consolidation tool, reporting repository — and pull the current access list for each.
Confirm no user can both post a Solvency UK valuation adjustment and approve it; take away any conflicting entitlement and record the removal ticket number.
Pull the change log for the reference period and confirm every change to a valuation rule or template mapping carries an approved change record.
Evidence that the reporting extracts run from production, not a copied environment, by capturing the source database identifier on the extract header.
checklist.done: access, change and extract-source evidence exists for every system in the chain with no unresolved segregation conflict.

checklist.step: Run the data quality controls on the inputs the templates depend on
actions: Run the completeness, accuracy and appropriateness rule set over the policy, claims, asset and reinsurance extracts feeding the templates, as required by Conditions Governing Business 6 for data used in technical provisions.
Record the record counts and control totals at extract, at transformation and at template load, and prove the three agree.
Investigate every rule breach above the defined tolerance with the source data owner and record either a correction or an accepted data limitation with its quantified effect.
Publish the data quality report and reference it from the SFCR Section D valuation narrative.
checklist.done: the data quality report is published, control totals agree across all three stages, and every accepted limitation is quantified.

checklist.step: Control the drafting of the Section A-E narrative against the prescribed structure
actions: Draft each section against the PS3/24 prescribed headings so a reader can find business and performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation for solvency purposes and capital management in the mandated order.
For every quantitative sentence in the narrative, put the source template cell reference into a hidden tie-out column — no number may appear in the text without a template source.
Draft Part 1 in plain English for policyholders and confirm it carries no number that contradicts Part 2.
Send the draft to the Appointed Actuary (Section D), the Chief Risk Officer (Section C) and the Corporate Secretary (Section B) for section owner sign-off.
checklist.done: both SFCR parts follow the prescribed structure, every quantitative statement carries a template cell reference, and each section owner has signed.

checklist.step: Control late journals, topside entries and manual template overrides
actions: Extract every journal posted after the week-6 balance sheet lock and every manual override applied directly to a template cell.
Require a written rationale, a preparer and an independent approver for each — self-approved post-lock entries are rejected and reversed.
Re-run the GL-to-S.02.01 reconciliation after the last post-lock entry so the filed figures reflect the final ledger.
List the post-lock population and its net effect on own funds and the SCR ratio for the Audit Committee pack.
checklist.done: every post-lock entry and override is rationalised and independently approved, and the reconciliation has been re-run afterwards.

checklist.step: Perform the movement analysis review control over the solvency position
actions: Build the year-on-year movement analysis of own funds and the SCR: new business strain, experience variances, assumption changes, market movements, the matching adjustment and any transitional recalculation.
Set an investigation threshold of 5% of opening eligible own funds and explain every movement above it with a named driver and an owner.
Compare the closing SCR coverage ratio to the risk appetite range set by the board and flag any breach to the Chief Risk Officer the same day.
Present the analysis at the pre-close review meeting and minute the challenge and responses.
checklist.done: every movement above the 5% threshold has a named driver, and the coverage ratio has been compared to board risk appetite with the review minuted.

checklist.step: Enforce the evidence standard on every matrix control
actions: For each matrix row, collect the evidence pack: the input used, the work performed, the reviewer's challenge and the dated sign-off.
Reject evidence that shows only an outcome — a screenshot of a completed template proves nothing about the control that produced it.
Confirm every sign-off date sits on or before the gate date on the close calendar and log any late sign-off as an exception immediately.
Index the packs by matrix row id in the compliance evidence repository under the reference date.
checklist.done: every matrix row has an indexed evidence pack showing input, performance, review and a sign-off dated on or before its gate.

checklist.step: Run the external audit interface for the relevant elements of the SFCR
actions: Agree with the external auditor the scope of the audited relevant elements — the valuation for solvency purposes and capital management sections plus templates S.02.01, S.12.01, S.23.01 and S.25.01 as applicable to the firm.
Deliver the prepared-by-client list on the agreed dates and log every audit request and response in the audit request tracker.
Resolve audit differences before the week-9 gate: post the adjustment or record the auditor's uncorrected difference and its effect on eligible own funds.
Obtain the auditor's report on the relevant elements for annexing to the SFCR.
checklist.done: the audit of the relevant elements is complete by the week-9 gate and the auditor's report is in hand for annexing.

checklist.step: Take the SFCR to the board for approval before submission
actions: Load the final SFCR Parts 1 and 2, the auditor's report on the relevant elements and the control deficiency summary to the board portal at least five business days before the week-12 meeting.
Table the administrative, management or supervisory body's approval resolution and confirm the directors' statement on the SFCR is included in the pack.
Minute the approval with the version identifier of the document approved so a later amendment cannot pass as the approved text.
Release the approved version to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for PRA submission and to Communications for website publication.
checklist.done: the board has approved a named SFCR version, the approval is minuted with that version id, and the approved file has been released for submission and publication.

checklist.step: Log deficiencies and drive them to closure before the next reference date
actions: Raise every failed or late matrix control as a deficiency record with severity, affected template, root cause category (data, model handoff, access, timetable, judgement) and an owner.
Set remediation dates that land before the next year-end kick-off and require a design change, not a promise to be more careful.
Report the deficiency population and ageing to the Audit Committee each quarter.
Re-test every closed deficiency in the following cycle and reopen anything that recurs.
checklist.done: every deficiency carries severity, root cause, owner and a remediation date before the next kick-off, with quarterly Audit Committee reporting.

testing.step: Build the population of controls and template lines the matrix claims to cover
actions: Export the approved SFCR control matrix version for the reference date and count the rows by control type (data, valuation, disclosure, ITGC).
Independently list every line in S.02.01, S.12.01, S.23.01 and S.25.01 and map it to the matrix row that assures it.
Report unassured template lines as a coverage gap before any sampling begins — an untested gap is worse than a failed control.
Sign the population as complete with the matrix version id and export timestamp.
testing.done: the population is signed, the matrix version is identified, and every unassured template line is listed as a coverage gap.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed SFCR back to the frozen ledger and the registered model run
actions: Pull the trial balance as at the freeze timestamp and re-add the Solvency UK valuation bridge to an independent S.02.01.
Compare your S.02.01 to the filed template line by line and investigate every difference, not only those above the posting tolerance.
Trace the technical provisions in the filed S.12.01 to the model run identifier registered in the model governance repository and confirm the run date precedes the handoff sign-off.
Record the reconciliation with both source references in the workpaper.
testing.done: the filed S.02.01 and S.12.01 reconcile to the frozen ledger and a registered model run, with every difference explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the control sample
actions: Test 100% of controls rated key over the solvency balance sheet, own funds tiering and the SCR.
Select 25 further controls at random using a recorded seed from the remaining matrix rows, minimum 40 controls in total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every deficiency carried forward from the prior cycle as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed, covers all key controls and includes every prior-cycle deficiency.

testing.step: Re-perform the own funds tiering and the EPIFP calculation independently
actions: Take the subordinated instrument terms sheets and reach your own tier conclusion against the Own Funds Part conditions before reading the preparer's conclusion.
Recompute EPIFP by revaluing the best estimate with future premiums set to nil and compare your result to the figure in S.23.01 row R0790.
Recompute the tiering eligibility limits against the SCR and MCR and confirm the restricted amounts in the filed template.
Treat a correct number reached on an unsupported basis as an exception, the same as a wrong number.
testing.done: tiering and the R0790 EPIFP figure have been independently re-derived and agreed, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the SCR standard formula assembly on the sampled modules
actions: Rebuild the Basic SCR from the module results using the prescribed correlation matrices in an independent workbook.
Recompute the operational risk charge and the loss-absorbing capacity of deferred taxes, and test the LACDT against the deferred tax liability recognised in S.02.01.
Recompute the MCR linear result and check the floor and cap against the SCR are applied in the filed S.28.
Recompute the SCR coverage ratio quoted in SFCR Section E from the annexed templates.
testing.done: the SCR, MCR and the coverage ratio quoted in Section E have been independently recomputed and agree with the filed templates.

testing.step: Trace narrative statements in the SFCR to their template source
actions: Take 20 quantitative statements across Sections A-E and the Part 1 policyholder summary.
Trace each to the cited template cell and confirm the figure, the basis and the period label match.
Confirm Part 1 states nothing that contradicts Part 2, particularly on the SCR coverage ratio and any capital management action.
Flag every statement with no traceable source, including rounded or 'approximately' figures.
testing.done: all 20 sampled statements trace to a template cell with matching basis and period, and Part 1 is consistent with Part 2.

testing.step: Test evidence quality and timing on every sampled control
actions: Open the evidence pack for each sampled control and confirm it shows the input used, the work performed, the reviewer's challenge and a dated sign-off.
Compare the sign-off date to the close calendar gate date and fail anything signed after its gate.
Reject outcome-only evidence such as a screenshot of a completed template with no evidence of performance.
Test that the retention label on each pack is the 10-year label required for SFCR evidence.
testing.done: each sampled control has performance evidence signed on or before its gate and carries the 10-year retention label.

testing.step: Test the post-lock journal and override population in full
actions: Extract 100% of journals posted after the balance sheet freeze timestamp and every manual template override.
Confirm each has a written rationale, a preparer and a different approver — any self-approved entry is an exception without exception.
Recompute the net effect of the post-lock population on eligible own funds and the SCR ratio and compare it to the figure reported to the Audit Committee.
Confirm the GL-to-S.02.01 reconciliation was re-run after the last post-lock entry.
testing.done: no post-lock entry is self-approved or unrationalised, and the reported post-lock effect on own funds recomputes.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, severity and owner
actions: Raise one record per exception naming the matrix row, the template affected and the effect on the reported solvency position.
Rate severity as deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness using the balance sheet / own funds / SCR escalation rule, and assign a root cause and owner.
For any material weakness, open a Fundamental Rule 7 notification assessment with the Chief Risk Officer before the SFCR is published.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception is rated, root-caused, owned and dated, with a notification assessment opened for any material weakness.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the control failure rate and the significant deficiency count and compare them to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the reviewer, who owns and performs no control in the SFCR matrix, sign the workpaper and date it.
Report the conclusion and any material weakness to the Audit Committee before the board approves the SFCR, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, failure rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed before board approval of the SFCR.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual programme that tests the key controls over the Solvency UK regulatory returns (UK QRTs and National Specific Templates) and drives deficiency remediation to closure; reports directly to the Audit Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Reporting Part read with PS15/24 'Review of Solvency II: Reporting phase 2' (reduced template set and revised solo deadlines of 30 business days quarterly / 70 business days annually, applying from the 31 December 2024 reference date), plus Conditions Governing Business (ORSA) and the Reporting Part (SFCR) as amended by PS3/24; citation refreshed each January against the PRA Rulebook Online snapshot

In-scope processes.value: Controls over the quarterly and annual PRA return production run only: data extraction, template population for the reduced UK QRT set and the National Specific Templates, validation rule clearance, sign-off and BEEDS submission — plus the deficiency remediation loop that follows

In-scope systems.value: The regulatory reporting engine that builds the UK QRTs and NSTs and produces the XBRL instance submitted through the Bank of England BEEDS portal; source data comes from the enterprise data warehouse and the actuarial modelling platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Returns Control Testing Programme — the key control listing per template family (S.02, S.06 asset line-by-line, S.12/S.17 technical provisions, S.23 own funds, S.25 SCR, S.28 MCR, NS.00-NS.10 national templates), the test plan per control, sampling rules and the deficiency rating scale

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee as part of the annual internal audit plan; re-approved whenever the PRA changes the template set or a deadline, and on any change of reporting engine

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The controls under test serve deadlines of 30 business days after each quarter-end and 70 business days after the 31 December annual reference date for a solo UK insurer (41 and 82 business days at group level); the audit is scheduled to conclude before the annual submission so deficiencies can be corrected in-cycle

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit milestones sit on the same return calendar as the reporting run, with alerts at submission minus 25 business days (fieldwork complete) and minus 10 business days (deficiencies communicated); the reporting engine's own validation-rule countdown is monitored in parallel

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Test programme, control walkthroughs, sampled evidence, validation-rule clearance logs, BEEDS submission receipts and the remediation tracker retained 10 years from the reference date in AuditBoard with a copy in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each control failure becomes an audit finding rated critical / high / medium with the template affected, the misstatement or late-submission risk it creates, an accountable owner and an agreed remediation date; resubmissions to the PRA are tracked as separate items

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off closure of critical and high findings; Internal Audit validates closure by re-performing the control before the finding is marked closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every UK QRT and National Specific Template submitted for the four quarterly reference dates and the annual reference date in the year, together with the key controls listed against each template family in the control listing

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any return submitted after the 30 / 70 business day deadline is an automatic critical finding; any template with an unexplained cleared blocking validation rule, or a value that cannot be re-derived from source within a 0.5% tolerance on technical provisions and 0.1% on own funds, is a high finding; two or more high findings in one template family means the family is rated ineffective

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation reports quarterly and annually; the control test runs annually over a population spanning all five submissions, with a targeted interim walkthrough after the Q2 return so design failures are caught before the annual run

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Testing is performed by Internal Audit staff who have never prepared, reviewed or submitted a UK QRT or NST; the Chief Audit Executive signs the conclusion

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual 'Solvency UK regulatory returns' audit file in AuditBoard — control listing, walkthroughs, samples, re-derivation workbooks, findings and the remediation tracker — indexed by reference date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Audit report, findings register and remediation status producible for the PRA supervisory team or a s166 skilled person review within 5 business days, with BEEDS submission receipts and validation logs attached

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers PRA data queries through the supervisory contact; any error requiring a resubmission is notified to the PRA supervisor with the corrected instance, and the Chief Risk Officer assesses Fundamental Rule 7 notification for material misreporting

checklist.step: Refresh the key control listing against the PS15/24 template set
actions: Pull the current UK QRT and National Specific Template list from the PRA Rulebook Reporting Part and the PS15/24 annexes, and mark the templates deleted in the reduction (roughly a third of the former Solvency II set).
Retire control rows that only served deleted templates and write new rows for the new and amended national templates.
Rank each remaining template family by misstatement risk to the reported solvency position and mark the controls that are key.
Table the refreshed listing at the Audit Committee with the annual audit plan and record its approval.
checklist.done: the control listing matches the current template set, deleted templates carry no orphan controls, and the Audit Committee has approved it.

checklist.step: Walk through the return production run end to end
actions: Sit with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst through one full quarterly run: source extract, load into the reporting engine, template population, validation, sign-off, XBRL generation, BEEDS upload.
Record at each hop who performs it, what system screen they use, what evidence falls out and where it is filed.
Identify hops with no control — commonly the manual spreadsheet that bridges the asset extract into S.06.02 line-by-line data.
Write the walkthrough narrative and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager confirm it describes what actually happens.
checklist.done: a confirmed end-to-end narrative exists identifying every hop, its control and any uncontrolled manual bridge.

checklist.step: Test controls over the source data extracts
actions: For each reference date, obtain the extract job logs and confirm the extracts ran against production at the reference date with no partial or re-run without approval.
Compare record counts and control totals at extract, transformation and template load, and confirm the three agree in the run's data reconciliation sheet.
Test that the data quality rule set defined under Conditions Governing Business 6 ran and that every breach was dispositioned by the source data owner.
Sample 10 policy and 10 asset records and trace each attribute end to end into the template it feeds.
checklist.done: extract logs, control totals and rule dispositions exist for every reference date and the 20 traced records agree end to end.

checklist.step: Test the validation rule clearance control
actions: Export the validation rule results for each submission, split into blocking and non-blocking rules.
For every rule failure that was cleared rather than fixed, read the recorded justification and confirm it was approved by someone other than the preparer.
Fail any clearance justified only as 'known issue' or 'accepted by the business' with no analysis of the value effect.
Confirm the final XBRL instance uploaded to BEEDS carries zero outstanding blocking failures.
checklist.done: every cleared validation failure has an independently approved, quantified justification and no blocking failure survived into the submitted instance.

checklist.step: Re-derive key template values independently from source
actions: Take the technical provisions in S.12.01 and S.17.01, own funds in S.23.01 and the SCR in S.25.01 for the annual reference date.
Rebuild each figure from the underlying model output and ledger extract in an independent workbook without using the reporting engine.
Compare against the submitted values using the 0.5% technical provisions and 0.1% own funds tolerances and list every breach.
Where a difference exists, walk it back to the specific mapping, aggregation or override that caused it.
checklist.done: the four key template values re-derive within tolerance or the causing mapping or override is identified.

checklist.step: Test the National Specific Template controls separately
actions: List the NSTs the firm is required to submit for its business — including matching adjustment asset and liability data and business model analysis templates — and confirm none has been omitted on the assumption it was deleted.
For each NST, test that the preparer used the current PRA template version and instructions, not a prior year's spreadsheet.
Trace a sample of five lines per NST back to source and confirm the definitions applied match the PRA instructions rather than internal management reporting definitions.
Flag any NST prepared entirely in a spreadsheet outside the reporting engine as an elevated risk control gap.
checklist.done: every required NST is submitted on the current template version with five lines traced to source per template.

checklist.step: Test the sign-off and submission controls
actions: Obtain the sign-off sheet for each of the five submissions and confirm the preparer, reviewer and approver are three different people with the approver at or above Regulatory Reporting Manager level.
Confirm each sign-off is dated before the BEEDS upload timestamp on the submission receipt.
Match the file hash or instance identifier on the receipt to the version that was signed off — a signed-off file that is not the submitted file is a critical finding.
Confirm access to submit through BEEDS is limited to named, approved users and reconcile that list to HR leavers.
checklist.done: each submission has three-party sign-off dated before upload, matching instance identifiers, and a clean BEEDS submitter access list.

checklist.step: Recompute the business-day deadline for every submission
actions: For each reference date, count forward 30 business days (quarterly) or 70 business days (annual) using the England and Wales business day calendar including bank holidays.
Record the computed deadline next to the BEEDS receipt timestamp and compute the days of headroom or lateness.
Where the firm reports at group level as well, repeat with the 41 and 82 business day group deadlines.
Escalate any submission with fewer than three business days of headroom as a process capacity risk, not just a near miss.
checklist.done: every submission has a recomputed deadline, an actual submission timestamp and a stated headroom, with sub-three-day headroom escalated.

checklist.step: Test the resubmission and correction control
actions: List every resubmission made to the PRA during the year and the reason for each.
Confirm each resubmission was notified to the PRA supervisory contact and that the corrected instance replaced the original in the reporting archive.
Test that the error that triggered the resubmission generated a control change, not only a corrected file.
Check whether the same template family has resubmitted more than once — a repeat is evidence the first remediation failed.
checklist.done: every resubmission is notified, archived and linked to a control change, and repeat resubmissions are flagged.

checklist.step: Rate every control failure and write the findings
actions: Write one finding per failed control naming the template, the reference date, what failed and the misstatement or late-filing exposure created.
Rate critical (missed deadline, submitted unsigned, material misstatement), high (unexplained cleared blocking rule, out-of-tolerance re-derivation) or medium (evidence or timing weakness).
Quantify the effect on the reported SCR coverage ratio wherever a value is wrong.
Issue the draft findings to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Controller for management response.
checklist.done: every failure has a rated, quantified finding issued for management response.

checklist.step: Agree remediation actions with owners and dates
actions: For each finding, write a remediation action that changes the design — a new automated reconciliation, a removed manual bridge, an added approver — rather than a promise of extra care.
Name a single accountable owner and a date that lands before the next reference date the control serves.
Where remediation cannot land in time, record the compensating control that will run in the interim and who performs it.
Return the responses to Internal Audit for acceptance; audit may reject an action it judges will not fix the cause.
checklist.done: every finding has an accepted design-change action, an owner and a date before the next affected reference date.

checklist.step: Track remediation to closure and validate it
actions: Maintain the remediation tracker with status, ageing and overdue flags per finding.
Before closing any critical or high finding, re-perform the changed control over a live return run and keep the evidence.
Reopen any finding whose remediation is evidenced only by an updated procedure document with no operating evidence.
Report overdue critical and high findings to the Audit Committee monthly.
checklist.done: no critical or high finding is closed without re-performance evidence, and overdue items are reported monthly.

checklist.step: Escalate systemic weakness to the Audit Committee and the PRA where required
actions: Review the finding population for systemic themes — a template family rated ineffective, repeated resubmissions, chronic deadline headroom below three days.
Assess whether the weakness makes previously submitted returns materially unreliable and therefore notifiable under Fundamental Rule 7.
Where notifiable, prepare the notification to the PRA supervisory contact with the affected reference dates, the effect on reported figures and the remediation plan.
Record the assessment and its conclusion even where no notification is made.
checklist.done: a documented notification assessment exists for every systemic theme, with a notification issued where the threshold is met.

checklist.step: Report the annual conclusion to the Audit Committee
actions: Write the audit opinion on the control environment over Solvency UK regulatory returns with the rating per template family.
Include the deadline headroom analysis across all five submissions and the resubmission history for the year.
Present at the Audit Committee, minute the challenge and record the committee's acceptance of the remediation plan.
Share the report with the external auditor to support their work on the relevant elements of the SFCR.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has received and minuted the opinion, ratings and remediation plan for the reporting year.

checklist.step: Retain the audit file for the retention period
actions: Lock the audit file in AuditBoard so workpapers cannot be edited after the report date, and record the lock date.
Copy the report, findings register, remediation tracker and BEEDS receipts into the compliance evidence repository under the reference date.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the record is searchable by reference date, template code and finding rating.
Confirm the file can be produced to a PRA skilled person on demand.
checklist.done: the audit file is locked, copied, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by template code.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions and controls to be verified
actions: Extract from the reporting engine every UK QRT and NST instance submitted for the four quarterly and the annual reference dates, with submission timestamps.
Independently list the templates the firm is required to submit from the PRA Rulebook Reporting Part and PS15/24 annexes.
Compare the two lists and treat any required template with no submitted instance as a critical exception before sampling.
Sign the population with the extract timestamp and the rulebook snapshot date used.
testing.done: the submitted population is reconciled to the required template list and signed with both source dates.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit's control listing to the actual production run
actions: Compare the audit's key control listing to the walkthrough narrative of the live run.
Identify hops in the live run that carry no listed control — particularly manual spreadsheet bridges into S.06.02 and the NSTs.
Confirm every control the listing calls key genuinely prevents or detects a misstatement, rather than merely recording that work happened.
Log unlisted hops as scope exceptions against the audit, not against the reporting team.
testing.done: every production hop is either covered by a listed key control or logged as an audit scope exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across submissions and template families
actions: Take 100% of controls over S.02.01, S.12.01, S.23.01, S.25.01 and S.28 for the annual reference date.
Select 20 further control instances at random with a recorded seed across the four quarterly submissions and the NSTs.
Record the seed, population size and draw date so the selection can be reproduced.
Add every prior-year critical and high finding as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all annual key templates and includes all prior-year critical and high findings.

testing.step: Re-perform the deadline computation for all five submissions
actions: Recount 30 business days from each quarterly reference date and 70 business days from 31 December on the England and Wales business day calendar.
Compare each computed deadline to the BEEDS submission receipt timestamp and record headroom or lateness in days.
Repeat with the 41 and 82 business day group deadlines where a group return is filed.
Any submission after its deadline is a critical exception regardless of whether the PRA raised it.
testing.done: all five deadlines are independently recomputed and each submission's headroom or lateness is stated in days.

testing.step: Independently re-derive a sampled template value from source
actions: Pick two sampled template values — one technical provisions line and one own funds line — for the annual reference date.
Rebuild each from the warehouse extract and the model output without using the reporting engine or the audit's own workbook.
Compare to the submitted figure against the 0.5% and 0.1% tolerances and to the audit team's re-derivation.
A difference between your figure and the audit team's figure is an exception against the audit, and must be reconciled line by line.
testing.done: both values re-derive within tolerance and agree with the audit team's re-derivation, or the difference is reconciled.

testing.step: Test cleared validation rules on the sampled submissions
actions: Pull the validation rule log for each sampled submission and list every failure that was cleared rather than corrected.
Read each justification and confirm it names the value effect and was approved by someone other than the preparer.
Confirm the submitted XBRL instance carried zero outstanding blocking failures.
Compare your list to the audit's — a cleared failure the audit did not test is an audit coverage exception.
testing.done: every cleared failure on the sampled submissions is quantified, independently approved and was tested by the audit.

testing.step: Trace sign-off evidence and submitted-file identity
actions: For each sampled submission, open the sign-off sheet and confirm preparer, reviewer and approver are three distinct named individuals.
Confirm each signature date precedes the BEEDS upload timestamp on the receipt.
Match the instance identifier or file hash on the receipt to the signed-off version and fail any mismatch outright.
Reconcile the BEEDS submitter access list to the HR leaver report for the year.
testing.done: every sampled submission shows three-party pre-upload sign-off, a matching instance identifier and no leaver retaining submit access.

testing.step: Test whether remediation actually changed the control
actions: Take every finding closed during the year and open its closure evidence.
Confirm the evidence shows the changed control operating on a live return run, not just a revised procedure document.
Re-perform the changed control on one instance yourself and compare the outcome to the closure evidence.
Reopen any finding where the same failure mode recurs in a later reference date.
testing.done: every closed finding is supported by live operating evidence and one re-performed instance, with recurrences reopened.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, rating and owner
actions: Raise one record per exception with the reference date, template code, control id and the exposure created.
Assign a root cause category — coverage gap, manual bridge, sign-off timing, validation clearance, deadline capacity — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next reference date the control serves and note the interim compensating control.
Carry all open exceptions into next year's test population as mandatory rows.
testing.done: every exception carries a root cause, owner, remediation date and next-cycle retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the exception rate by template family and compare it to the two-high-findings ineffective threshold.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references behind each rating.
Have the reviewer, who has never prepared, reviewed or submitted a UK QRT or NST, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, deadline headroom and open critical findings to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the per-family conclusion and exception rate and has been reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Refresh the independence policy against the current Ethical Standard
actions: Read the current FRC Revised Ethical Standard sections on fees, non-audit services and rotation as they apply to a Public Interest Entity insurer.
Update the permitted services whitelist and the prohibited list in the policy, marking each change with the Standard paragraph that drove it.
Confirm the policy explicitly covers services supplied to the firm by any network firm of the auditor, in any jurisdiction.
Table the revised policy at the Audit Committee for approval and record the minute reference in the policy header.
checklist.done: the policy reflects the current Ethical Standard paragraph by paragraph and carries an Audit Committee approval minute reference.

checklist.step: Block the audit firm and its network on the supplier master
actions: Flag the statutory audit firm and every network firm entity in the supplier master with an approval-required rule.
Configure the requisition workflow so any requisition naming a flagged supplier routes to the Corporate Secretary before it can be approved.
Test the block by raising a dummy requisition against a network firm and confirming it stops.
Reconcile the flagged entity list to the audit firm's published network member list at least annually.
checklist.done: no requisition to the audit firm or a network firm can proceed without routing to the Corporate Secretary, proven by a test requisition.

checklist.step: Assess each proposed non-audit service against the whitelist before engagement
actions: Take the service description from the sponsoring business owner and classify it as audit, audit-related assurance, other assurance or non-audit service.

Test it against the PIE permitted services whitelist and reject anything not on it — including bookkeeping, valuation services feeding the financial statements, internal audit outsourcing, tax services involving advocacy and any service involving management decision-making.
Assess the threat created (self-review, self-interest, advocacy, familiarity, management) and name the safeguard, or conclude no safeguard is sufficient.
Write the assessment onto the pre-approval request with the whitelist reference relied on.
checklist.done: each proposed service carries a written classification, whitelist reference, threat assessment and named safeguard, or a rejection.

checklist.step: Obtain Audit Committee pre-approval before any engagement letter is signed
actions: Table the pre-approval request at the Audit Committee, or use the delegated authority route where the committee has set a de minimis threshold and a standing category list.
Record the committee decision in the minutes naming the service, the fee, the threat and the safeguard.
Release the approval reference to Procurement so the requisition can proceed; no reference, no purchase order.
Report all delegated approvals to the next full committee meeting for ratification.
checklist.done: no engagement letter is signed without a minuted pre-approval reference, and delegated approvals are ratified at the next meeting.

checklist.step: Maintain the audit-firm fee register split by service category
actions: Run a vendor spend report for the audit firm and every network firm covering purchase orders, invoices and accruals for the financial year.
Split each amount into statutory audit, audit of the relevant elements of the SFCR, other audit-related assurance, and non-audit services, and tag the entity that received the service.
Investigate any spend with no matching pre-approval reference and treat it as an exception the day it is found.
Reconcile the register to the fee note disclosed in the annual report so the two cannot diverge.
checklist.done: the fee register is complete by category and entity, every line carries a pre-approval reference, and it reconciles to the annual report fee note.

checklist.step: Compute and monitor the 70% non-audit fee cap
actions: Take the statutory audit fees for the preceding three consecutive financial years and compute their average.
Sum the non-audit service fees for the current year on the basis required by the Ethical Standard, excluding services required by law or regulation.
Express the current-year non-audit fees as a percentage of the three-year average audit fee and record it monthly.
Raise an alert to the Corporate Secretary at 50% and freeze all further non-audit engagement at 70%.
checklist.done: the cap ratio is recomputed monthly on the three-year average basis, with alerts at 50% and a hard freeze at 70%.

checklist.step: Maintain the key audit partner and reviewer rotation register
actions: Record for the key audit partner, the engagement quality control reviewer and every other partner in a significant role: name, role, first year on the engagement and the year they must rotate off.
Apply the five-year limit with a five-year cooling-off for the key audit partner on a PIE, and the applicable limit for the engagement quality reviewer.
Ask the audit firm each year to confirm the register against its own records in writing and reconcile any difference.
Raise an alert 18 months before any limit so succession and shadowing can be planned with the committee.
checklist.done: the register is confirmed in writing by the audit firm, shows the rotation-off year for every significant-role partner, and alerts 18 months ahead.

checklist.step: Track the firm tendering and rotation clocks
actions: Record the date the current audit firm was first appointed and compute the mandatory tender year at ten years and the mandatory rotation year at twenty.
Report the elapsed tenure and the two clock dates in the Audit Committee report within the annual report each year.
Start tender planning at least 18 months before the tender year, and include a report on why the incumbent was or was not retained.
Record the board resolution proposing the auditor for reappointment at the AGM, with the committee's recommendation attached.
checklist.done: tenure, tender year and rotation year are recorded, disclosed annually, and tender planning starts 18 months ahead.

checklist.step: Collect the auditor's written independence confirmations at both required points
actions: Before the engagement letter is signed, obtain the firm's written confirmation of independence covering the firm, the network and all covered persons.
Before the audit opinion is signed, obtain the ISA (UK) 260 communication confirming independence, listing all relationships and services and the safeguards applied.
Compare the services listed by the auditor to your own fee register — a service on their list and not on yours means a pre-approval was bypassed.
File both confirmations to the Audit Committee papers with the fee register attached.
checklist.done: two dated independence confirmations exist per year and the auditor's service list reconciles to the internal fee register.

checklist.step: Control employment relationships that create familiarity or self-review threats
actions: Screen every hire into Finance, Actuarial, Risk and Internal Audit for prior employment at the audit firm within the cooling-off period.
Where a former member of the audit team is hired into a role with financial reporting influence, notify the Corporate Secretary before the offer is made.
Maintain the register of employees who left to join the audit firm and of audit firm partners appointed to the board or a senior management function.
Report the register to the Audit Committee annually alongside the independence confirmations.
checklist.done: every relevant hire and leaver is screened and registered, with pre-offer notification for anyone from the audit team.

checklist.step: Protect the independence of the SFCR relevant-elements audit specifically
actions: Confirm the audit firm supplies no service that would put it in the position of auditing its own work on the Solvency UK balance sheet, technical provisions or own funds.
Reject any proposal for the audit firm to build, calibrate or validate the models or the valuation overlay that feed the audited templates.
Where the firm supplies permitted actuarial-adjacent assurance, record the separation of teams and the safeguard the firm has applied.
Record this specific assessment in the pre-approval file for each engagement touching Solvency UK reporting.
checklist.done: no engagement puts the auditor in a self-review position over the audited relevant elements of the SFCR, and the assessment is filed per engagement.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate any independence breach immediately
actions: On discovery, log the breach with the date, the service or relationship, the threat category and the fee involved, and notify the Audit Committee Chair the same day.
Ask the audit firm for its own assessment of whether objectivity was compromised and what safeguard it applied.
Agree the remediation: terminate the service, replace the engagement team, or where objectivity cannot be restored, consider whether the opinion can be signed at all.
Record the committee's conclusion and the reasoning in the minutes before the audit opinion date.
checklist.done: every breach has a same-day escalation, the firm's own assessment, an agreed remediation and a minuted committee conclusion before the opinion date.

checklist.step: Disclose the independence position in the annual report
actions: Draft the Audit Committee report section covering auditor tenure, the tender and rotation clocks, the policy on non-audit services and the fees paid by category.
State the committee's conclusion that the auditor remained independent and objective, and the basis on which it reached that conclusion.
Tie every fee figure in the disclosure to the fee register and the financial statements fee note.
Route the drafted section to the Audit Committee Chair for approval before the annual report is signed.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee report discloses tenure, clocks, policy, fees by category and a reasoned independence conclusion, approved by the Chair.

checklist.step: Assess the auditor's effectiveness and recommend reappointment or replacement
actions: Run the annual audit quality assessment: survey Finance, Actuarial and Internal Audit on scepticism, technical challenge on technical provisions and timeliness.
Read the FRC Audit Quality Review findings on the firm and on the insurance sector and ask the engagement partner to respond to them.
Combine with the tenure position and write the committee's recommendation on reappointment.
Present the recommendation to the board for the AGM resolution and minute the decision.
checklist.done: a documented annual effectiveness assessment supports a minuted reappointment or replacement recommendation to the board.

checklist.step: File the independence evidence for the retention period
actions: Assemble the year's file: policy version, pre-approval log, engagement letters, fee register, cap computation, rotation register, both independence confirmations, employment screening register and the breach log.
Index it by financial year and by audit firm entity so a regulator can be given a single coherent file.
Apply the 10-year retention label.
Confirm the file is retrievable by service description and by partner name.
checklist.done: a single indexed independence file per financial year is retained for 10 years and retrievable by service and partner name.

testing.step: Build the population of audit-firm engagements and spend
actions: Extract all purchase orders, invoices, credit notes and accruals in the financial year where the supplier is the audit firm or any network firm, across every group entity.
Search the supplier master by name fragments as well as by supplier id so a network firm set up under a different code cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract total to the fee note in the financial statements and resolve every difference before sampling.
Sign the population with the extract date and the entity list covered.
testing.done: the spend population reconciles to the published fee note and is signed with its entity coverage.

testing.step: Reconcile the internal fee register to the auditor's own disclosed service list
actions: Take the service list in the auditor's ISA (UK) 260 independence communication.
Match line by line to the internal fee register on entity, service description and fee.
Any service the auditor discloses that the register does not hold is an automatic exception — it means the pre-approval gate was bypassed.
Any service the register holds that the auditor does not disclose is queried with the engagement partner in writing.
testing.done: the two service lists reconcile item by item, with every unmatched item raised as an exception or queried in writing.

testing.step: Draw the engagement sample and document it
actions: Take 100% of non-audit service engagements and 100% of engagements touching Solvency UK reporting.
Select 15 further audit-related and assurance engagements at random using a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population size and draw date so the sample can be redrawn.
Include every prior-year exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all non-audit and Solvency-UK-touching engagements, is reproducible, and includes prior-year exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the whitelist assessment on each sampled non-audit service
actions: Read the engagement letter scope and reach your own conclusion on whether the service is permitted for a PIE before reading the preparer's assessment.
Test specifically for prohibited categories: bookkeeping, valuation feeding the financial statements, internal audit outsourcing, tax advocacy, and any service involving management decisions.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded assessment; a right answer supported by the wrong Ethical Standard paragraph is still an exception.
Capture the engagement letter scope wording you relied on in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled service has an independent permissibility conclusion with the engagement letter wording captured.

testing.step: Trace every sampled engagement to a pre-approval that pre-dates it
actions: Match each sampled engagement to a pre-approval record and open the Audit Committee minute it cites.
Confirm the minute names the service, the fee and the safeguard, and that its date precedes the engagement letter date.
Where delegated authority was used, confirm the ratification appears in a subsequent minute.
Treat an approval dated after the engagement letter as a breach, not a documentation timing issue.
testing.done: every sampled engagement traces to a minuted pre-approval dated before its engagement letter, with delegated approvals ratified.

testing.step: Recompute the 70% fee cap independently
actions: Pull the statutory audit fee for each of the three preceding consecutive financial years from the signed accounts, not from the register.
Recompute the three-year average and the current-year non-audit fee total, applying the exclusions for services required by law or regulation and documenting each exclusion.
Recompute the ratio and compare it to the monitored figure; a difference over one percentage point is an exception.
Recompute the ratio again on a rolling basis at each quarter-end to confirm the freeze would have triggered at 70%.
testing.done: the cap ratio is independently recomputed from signed accounts at year-end and at each quarter-end and agrees with the monitored figure.

testing.step: Recompute partner tenure and cooling-off against the register
actions: For the key audit partner and the engagement quality reviewer, count consecutive years on the engagement from the audit firm's written confirmation, not from the internal register.
Compare to the five-year PIE limit for the key audit partner and the applicable reviewer limit; a sixth consecutive year is an automatic fail.
Where a partner has rotated, confirm the five-year cooling-off has been observed before any return to the engagement.
Recompute the firm tenure from the first appointment date and confirm the ten-year tender and twenty-year rotation years disclosed in the annual report.
testing.done: tenure and cooling-off are recomputed from the firm's written confirmation and agree with the register and the annual report disclosure.

testing.step: Test the procurement block actually stops unapproved spend
actions: Raise a test requisition against a network firm entity and confirm it routes to the Corporate Secretary and cannot be approved without a pre-approval reference.
Extract all requisitions to flagged suppliers in the year and confirm none was approved without a reference.
Reconcile the flagged entity list to the audit firm's published network member list and list any unflagged network entity.
Test whether spend was routed through an unflagged intermediary or a consortium arrangement.
testing.done: the block is proven by a live test requisition, no unreferenced approval exists, and every network entity is flagged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with threat category, root cause and owner
actions: Raise one record per exception naming the engagement, the entity, the fee and the threat category created.
Assign a root cause — supplier not flagged, delegated authority misused, whitelist misread, register not reconciled to the firm's confirmation — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the breach touches the audited relevant elements of the SFCR, escalate to the Chief Risk Officer for a Fundamental Rule 7 assessment.
Carry all open exceptions into the next quarterly test as mandatory rows.
testing.done: every exception carries a threat category, root cause, owner, remediation date and any required notification assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report before the opinion is signed
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance thresholds for unapproved services, prohibited services, cap breach and overdue rotation.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who neither requested nor sponsored any service from the audit firm in the year, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee before the audit opinion date so the committee can consider the position when it concludes on independence, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit Committee before the audit opinion is signed.

In-scope systems.value: Signed accounts, the auditor's reports and the filing receipts are version-controlled in the financial reporting repository; the accounts are filed to Companies House by iXBRL upload and the SFCR package is submitted through the Bank of England BEEDS portal

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Statutory accounts filed at Companies House within six months of the 31 December year-end for a public company (nine months for a private company); the SFCR with the auditor's report on the relevant elements submitted to the PRA and published within 14 weeks of the reference date; the auditor's written report to the PRA delivered by the date agreed with the supervisor where the firm meets the written auditor reporting threshold

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar tasks alert the Controller at T-30, T-10 and T-3 business days for each of the three filings; a separate alert fires on the Companies House filing deadline itself, and the BEEDS submission window is monitored daily in the final week
