Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A late filing, a rejected Companies House submission, a failed BEEDS upload or an unclosed auditor recommendation past its agreed date is logged with cause, exposure (including the civil penalty for late accounts) and a remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off closure of every significant deficiency raised in the auditor's ISA (UK) 265 communication and any late or amended filing

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The three annual filings for the reference year — Companies House accounts, the PRA SFCR package with the auditor's report on the relevant elements, and the auditor's written report to the PRA — plus every point raised in the ISA (UK) 260 report and the management letter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on lateness: any filing made after its statutory deadline is a fail. A filing whose content differs from the board-approved version is a fail. Any auditor recommendation still open beyond its agreed remediation date, or closed without evidence, is a fail; one fail escalates to the Audit Committee Chair

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual, so the test runs once per reporting year immediately after the last of the three filings, with a mid-year interim check on the ageing of open auditor recommendations

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit tests the filings; the reviewer must not have prepared, tagged, signed or submitted any of them

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual filing compliance test workpaper (deadline recomputation, receipt evidence, version comparison, auditor-point ageing) in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by financial year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed accounts, filing receipts, BEEDS confirmations and the auditor communications log producible for the PRA supervisory contact, the FRC or Companies House within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers PRA queries on the submitted package through the named supervisory contact; the Company Secretary handles Companies House correspondence and any late filing penalty appeal, and the CFO clears any restatement or amended filing before it is made

checklist.step: Build the annual filing calendar and name the signatories
actions: Enter the three deadlines against the 31 December reference date: Companies House accounts at six months, the SFCR package to the PRA at 14 weeks, and the auditor's written report to the PRA on the agreed date.

Name the signatory for each document: the director signing the balance sheet, the director signing the strategic report, the Corporate Secretary certifying the filing, and the Regulatory Reporting Manager submitting through BEEDS.
Back-schedule the internal gates: board approval date, auditor opinion date, iXBRL tagging complete date and BEEDS dry-run date.
Publish the calendar to Finance, Actuarial, Company Secretariat and the audit engagement team and record their acceptance.
checklist.done: the calendar carries all three statutory deadlines, named signatories and back-scheduled gates, accepted by every contributing team.

checklist.step: Finalise the statutory accounts for signature
actions: Produce the final financial statements from the consolidation tool after the last post-close adjustment and lock the reporting period.
Complete the disclosure checklist for an insurance entity: insurance contract liabilities, risk disclosures, capital management, related parties and the auditor fee note split by category.
Tie the auditor fee note to the audit-firm fee register held by the Corporate Secretary so the two disclosures cannot diverge.
Circulate the final draft to the Audit Committee five business days before the approval meeting.
checklist.done: the final accounts are produced from a locked period, the disclosure checklist is complete and the fee note ties to the independence fee register.

checklist.step: Obtain the auditor's opinion and the ISA (UK) 260 communication
actions: Receive the draft audit opinion and confirm the entity name, period, financial reporting framework and any key audit matters are correct.
Receive the ISA (UK) 260 report to those charged with governance and read the sections on significant findings, uncorrected misstatements, independence and management representations.
Prepare the schedule of uncorrected misstatements with the effect on profit, net assets and eligible own funds, and recommend correct or accept for each.
Sign the letter of representation only after every representation has been traced to underlying evidence.
checklist.done: the audit opinion, the ISA (UK) 260 report and a fully evidenced letter of representation are in hand before the board meeting.

checklist.step: Take the accounts and the auditor's report to the board for approval
actions: Load the final accounts, the draft audit opinion, the ISA (UK) 260 report and the uncorrected misstatements schedule to the board portal five business days before the meeting.
Table the going concern and viability assessment and the directors' responsibilities statement for approval alongside the accounts.
Minute the approval naming the document version approved and the directors authorised to sign.
Arrange signature of the balance sheet and the strategic report by the named directors on the approval date.
checklist.done: the board has approved a named version, the minute records the version and signatories, and the accounts are signed on the approval date.

checklist.step: Prepare and review the iXBRL tagging of the accounts
actions: Generate the iXBRL instance from the signed accounts using the current UK taxonomy applicable to the reporting framework.
Review the tagged primary statements element by element, and confirm entity identifier, period, currency and sign conventions are correct.
Run the validation and clear every error and every warning that changes the meaning of a tagged figure.
Render the instance back to human-readable form and compare it page by page to the signed PDF.
checklist.done: the iXBRL instance validates cleanly and renders identically to the signed accounts.

checklist.step: File the audited accounts with Companies House and capture the receipt
actions: Submit the signed accounts through the Companies House online filing service against the company registration number, well before the six-month deadline.
Confirm the submission is accepted rather than merely received — a rejection for an unsigned balance sheet or a missing auditor's report leaves the company unfiled.
Download the acceptance confirmation and the filed document from the public register and compare it to the board-approved version.
File the receipt, the acceptance email and the register copy into the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: Companies House shows the accounts as accepted, the public register copy matches the approved version, and the receipt is filed.

checklist.step: Assemble the SFCR package with the auditor's report on the relevant elements
actions: Assemble the package: SFCR Part 1 and Part 2, the annexed quantitative templates, and the auditor's report on the relevant elements of the SFCR required by the External Audit Part.
Confirm the auditor's report names the exact templates and sections within its scope and that they match the templates annexed.
Check the SFCR version is the one the board approved, by version identifier, not by file name.
Have the Controller confirm the package is complete before submission.
checklist.done: the package holds the board-approved SFCR version, the annexed templates and an auditor's report whose stated scope matches them.

checklist.step: Submit the SFCR package to the PRA and publish it
actions: Generate the submission files from the reporting engine and upload them through the Bank of England BEEDS portal against the correct return and reference date, at least three business days before the 14-week deadline.
Clear any portal validation failure and re-upload; a return left in a failed state is not submitted.
Download the BEEDS submission receipt showing the return, reference date and timestamp.
Publish the SFCR on the company website on or before the submission date and capture a dated screenshot of the published page.
checklist.done: BEEDS shows an accepted submission before the deadline and the SFCR is publicly available with dated evidence of publication.

checklist.step: Deliver the auditor's written report to the PRA where the firm is in scope
actions: Confirm with the PRA supervisory contact whether the firm meets the written auditor reporting threshold for the year and on which topics the report is required.
Agree the scope and the delivery date with the audit engagement partner and record both in the filing calendar.
Review the draft report for factual accuracy only — do not seek to influence the auditor's judgements, and record that boundary in the file.
Confirm the report was delivered to the PRA and file the auditor's confirmation of delivery.
checklist.done: the scope, date and delivery of the written auditor report are confirmed in writing, with the factual-accuracy boundary recorded.

checklist.step: Log every point in the management letter and the ISA (UK) 265 communication
actions: Enter each auditor point as its own record with the auditor's rating, the process affected and the auditor's recommendation quoted verbatim.
Attach management's response, a named owner and an agreed remediation date to each.
Cross-reference any point that also appears in the internal control matrix so the same weakness is not tracked twice with two different dates.
Report the population and its ageing to the Audit Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every auditor point is a tracked record with rating, verbatim recommendation, owner and agreed date, reported quarterly.

checklist.step: Close auditor recommendations with evidence, not assertion
actions: For each point due, collect evidence that the changed control has operated — a run log, a signed reconciliation, a system configuration screenshot.
Reject closure supported only by an updated procedure document or a statement that the issue no longer arises.
Ask the auditor to confirm at the following year's planning meeting whether it agrees the point is resolved, and record the answer.
Escalate any point overdue by more than 30 days to the Audit Committee Chair.
checklist.done: every closed point has operating evidence and an auditor confirmation, and overdue points are escalated at 30 days.

checklist.step: Reconcile the accounts to the Solvency UK reporting package
actions: Build the reconciliation from statutory net assets in the signed accounts to Solvency UK excess of assets over liabilities in S.02.01.
Explain each bridging item: valuation differences on investments and technical provisions, elimination of intangibles, deferred tax remeasurement and the risk margin.
Confirm the same reconciliation appears in SFCR Section D so the public and filed documents tell one story.
Have the Appointed Actuary confirm the technical provisions bridging items.
checklist.done: a signed bridge reconciles statutory net assets to Solvency UK own funds and matches the narrative in SFCR Section D.

checklist.step: Handle any amendment or restatement after filing
actions: Where an error is found after filing, quantify its effect on the accounts, on eligible own funds and on the SCR coverage ratio.
Decide with the General Counsel and the auditor whether revised accounts must be filed at Companies House and whether the SFCR must be resubmitted through BEEDS.
Notify the PRA supervisory contact before, not after, any resubmission of the SFCR package.
Record the decision, the notification and the corrected filing receipts in the same annual file.
checklist.done: any post-filing error has a quantified effect, a documented filing decision, a pre-emptive PRA notification and corrected receipts on file.

checklist.step: Report the completed filing position to the Audit Committee
actions: Present a filing status page showing each of the three filings, its statutory deadline, its actual date and the headroom in days.
Report the auditor point population by rating and ageing, and the uncorrected misstatements accepted.
Minute the committee's acknowledgement and any action it directs.
Carry any directed action into the remediation tracker with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: the committee has a minuted view of all three filings with headroom, plus auditor point ageing and directed actions.

checklist.step: Archive the annual filing file for retention
actions: Assemble the file: signed accounts, iXBRL instance, Companies House receipt and register copy, board minute, SFCR package and BEEDS receipts, auditor reports and the points log.
Index by financial year and by filing type so any single filing can be produced on its own.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the file is locked against edit after the archive date.
Test retrieval of one document from the prior year to prove the archive works.
checklist.done: the annual filing file is complete, indexed, locked, labelled for 10 years and retrieval-tested.

testing.step: Build the population of required filings and auditor communications
actions: List the filings required of the entity for the reference year from the Companies Act, the PRA Reporting Part and the External Audit Part, without reference to the filing calendar.
Compare your list to the calendar and treat any required filing absent from the calendar as a coverage exception.
List every auditor communication received in the year — engagement letter, ISA (UK) 260 report, management letter, written report to the PRA — and confirm each is on the points log.
Sign the population with the sources used.
testing.done: the independently derived filing and communication list reconciles to the calendar and points log, with gaps logged.

testing.step: Reconcile each filed document to the board-approved version
actions: Download the accounts from the Companies House public register and the SFCR from the company website.
Compare each to the version identifier recorded in the board minute, page by page on the primary statements and the annexed templates.
Any difference between the filed and approved documents is a fail, however immaterial the wording.
Confirm the auditor's report bound into the filed accounts is the signed version with the correct date.
testing.done: every filed document matches the board-approved version by identifier and content, with the signed auditor's report attached.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory deadline and the actual headroom
actions: Recompute the Companies House deadline as six months from the 31 December accounting reference date and compare it to the acceptance date on the register.
Recompute the SFCR deadline as 14 weeks from the reference date and compare it to the BEEDS receipt timestamp.
Recompute the agreed delivery date for the written auditor report and compare it to the auditor's delivery confirmation.
State the headroom or lateness in days for each and treat any negative figure as a fail.
testing.done: all three deadlines are independently recomputed and each filing's headroom or lateness is stated in days.

testing.step: Verify the filing receipts are acceptances, not acknowledgements
actions: Open the Companies House confirmation and confirm it records acceptance and appears on the public register, not merely a submission acknowledgement.
Open the BEEDS receipt and confirm the return code, reference date and status show an accepted submission with no outstanding validation failure.
Where any submission was rejected and resubmitted, obtain the rejection reason and confirm the final accepted date still met the deadline.
Capture each receipt into the workpaper.
testing.done: each filing is evidenced by an acceptance rather than an acknowledgement, with any rejection history reconciled to the deadline.

testing.step: Re-perform the iXBRL tagging review on a sample
actions: Select 25 tagged facts across the primary statements and the fee note using a recorded seed.
Compare each tagged element, value, sign, period and unit to the signed PDF.
Re-run the taxonomy validation on the filed instance and list any error or meaning-changing warning that was left uncleared.
Flag any figure present in the PDF but untagged where the taxonomy requires tagging.
testing.done: all 25 sampled facts agree with the signed accounts and the filed instance carries no uncleared meaning-changing validation issue.

testing.step: Test the auditor's report scope against the annexed templates
actions: Read the scope paragraph of the auditor's report on the relevant elements of the SFCR and list the sections and templates it names.
Compare that list to the templates actually annexed to the submitted SFCR package.
Any audited template missing from the package, or any package template outside the audit scope presented as audited, is an exception.
Confirm the report is addressed and dated as required and signed by the responsible partner.
testing.done: the auditor's stated scope matches the annexed templates exactly and the report is properly addressed, dated and signed.

testing.step: Re-perform the statutory-to-Solvency-UK own funds bridge
actions: Take net assets from the filed accounts and excess of assets over liabilities from the filed S.02.01.
Rebuild the bridge independently: investment valuation differences, technical provisions including the risk margin, intangibles written to nil and deferred tax remeasurement.
Compare your bridge to the reported one and to the narrative in SFCR Section D; a difference above 0.5% of own funds is an exception.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary's confirmation of the technical provisions bridging items is on file and dated before submission.
testing.done: the bridge re-derives within 0.5% of own funds and agrees with SFCR Section D, with a dated actuarial confirmation on file.

testing.step: Age the auditor points and test closure evidence
actions: Extract every ISA (UK) 260 and management letter point with its agreed date and current status.
Take 100% of points rated significant deficiency and 10 others at random and open their closure evidence.
Fail any closure supported only by a revised procedure document or a management assertion with no operating evidence.
Compare the open population to what was reported to the Audit Committee and flag any understatement.
testing.done: all significant deficiency points are evidence-tested, and the reported open population matches the tracker.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one record per exception naming the filing or auditor point, the deadline or date missed and the exposure created, including any Companies House late filing penalty band.
Assign a root cause — calendar gap, version control failure, tagging error, portal validation, closure without evidence — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next reporting year's equivalent gate.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, owner, quantified exposure and a remediation date before the next equivalent gate.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance lateness and version-difference thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who prepared, tagged, signed and submitted none of the filings, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the financial year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception count is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Chief Actuary (SIMF20) accountable for the Solvency UK technical provisions — best estimate liability, risk margin and any transitional measure — for the UK life and annuity portfolios each quarter and at the annual reference date

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Technical Provisions and Valuation Parts read with Solvency Capital Requirement – Standard Formula 3-5 and Reporting 3 (SFCR) as amended by PS3/24, plus the reformed risk margin (cost-of-capital rate reduced to 4% with the tapering factor) and the Matching Adjustment Part; the PRA technical information (risk-free rate term structures and fundamental spreads) is re-downloaded for each valuation date

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and annual technical provisions production for the UK life and annuity books: data extraction and validation → model point build → contract boundary and assumption setting → best estimate projection → matching adjustment and transitional application → risk margin calculation → reinsurance recoverables and counterparty default adjustment → sign-off into S.12.01 and S.02.01

In-scope systems.value: Licensed projection models run against locked model point files; every production run is registered with a run id in the model governance repository and results are handed to the reporting engine that builds S.12.01

Compliance procedure documented.value: Technical Provisions Valuation Manual — homogeneous risk group definitions, contract boundary rules, assumption-setting protocol, the PRA technical information download step, matching adjustment portfolio rules, the 4% cost-of-capital risk margin method with the taper, transitional recalculation triggers and the model run register

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and reviewed by the Model Risk Manager under the model governance framework; re-approved annually and on any PRA change to the risk margin, matching adjustment or transitional rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Results must be delivered to reporting in time for the 30 business day quarterly and 70 business day annual PRA deadlines: assumptions locked at reference date plus 10 business days, model run complete plus 20, actuarial sign-off plus 30 at year-end; the matching adjustment attestation and any transitional recalculation follow the annual cycle

Deadline reminders configured.value: Valuation calendar tasks alert the responsible actuary at each internal gate minus 3 business days; a standing alert fires when the PRA publishes the month-end technical information so the correct curve is picked up before the run

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Model point files, data validation reports, assumption papers with approval minutes, model run logs with run ids, results reconciliations, the risk margin workbook and the signed valuation report retained 10 years from the valuation date in the model governance repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every data limitation, model limitation, unapproved assumption, manual results adjustment and late gate is logged against the valuation date with its quantified effect on the best estimate and a disposition by the Chief Actuary

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs off the disposition of every logged limitation and any manual adjustment to model output before results are released to reporting

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All homogeneous risk groups valued at the reference date across the UK life and annuity portfolios, the model point files behind them, the assumption set applied, and the reconciliation from policy administration in-force to the valuation in-force

Pass/fail thresholds.value: In-force policy count and sum assured must reconcile from the administration system to the valuation extract within 0.1%; recomputed best estimate must fall within 0.5% of the reported figure per homogeneous risk group; the risk margin must recompute within 1%; any assumption applied without an approval minute, or any unlogged manual adjustment, is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The valuation runs quarterly and annually; testing runs quarterly on a reduced scope (data reconciliation and movement analysis) and in full at the annual reference date including independent recalculation

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Independent model validation is performed by the second-line model risk function; the reviewer may not have set assumptions, coded the model or run production for the valuation under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Technical provisions validation file per valuation date in the model governance repository — reconciliations, independent recalculation workbooks, assumption challenge log, findings and the validation opinion

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Valuation report, assumption papers, data quality report, model validation opinion and the reconciliation to S.12.01 producible within 5 business days for a PRA deep-dive, a matching adjustment review or a skilled person review

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Actuary answers PRA technical provisions questions through the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the supervisory contact; any restatement of technical provisions is notified before the corrected return is submitted

checklist.step: Extract and reconcile the in-force data at the valuation date
actions: Extract the in-force file at the valuation date with policy number, product code, annuity or sum assured amount, premium, commencement date, guarantee terms, and lives data including date of birth and gender.
Reconcile policy count, annuity in payment and sum assured to the administration system control report and to the prior quarter's valuation extract plus movements.
Investigate every difference above the 0.1% tolerance with the Policy Admin Ops Lead before the data is used.
Sign the data reconciliation sheet and attach it to the valuation folder for the reference date.
checklist.done: the valuation extract reconciles to the administration control report within 0.1% on count and amount, with a signed reconciliation on file.

checklist.step: Run the data quality assessment required for technical provisions
actions: Run the completeness, accuracy and appropriateness rule set over the extract as required by Conditions Governing Business 6 for data used in technical provisions.
Profile the critical fields for missing, defaulted or implausible values — dates of birth outside plausible ranges, zero annuity amounts, missing spouse data on joint-life annuities.
Quantify the effect of each unresolved deficiency on the best estimate and record it as a data limitation with a proxy or loading applied.
Publish the data quality report and reference it in the valuation report and SFCR Section D.
checklist.done: the data quality report is published, every unresolved deficiency is quantified, and the proxies applied are named.

checklist.step: Build and lock the model point file
actions: Group the in-force into homogeneous risk groups by product, guarantee type, matching adjustment eligibility and reinsurance arrangement.
Build the model points, applying grouping only where a grouping test shows the loss of information does not materially change the best estimate.
Reconcile model point totals back to the signed data extract on count, annuity amount and premium.
Lock the model point file, record its hash or version id, and register it against the valuation date.
checklist.done: a locked, version-identified model point file reconciles to the signed extract and its grouping is justified by a grouping test.

checklist.step: Set and approve the assumptions for the valuation date
actions: Prepare the assumption paper covering base mortality and improvements, longevity, lapse and paid-up rates, expenses with the expense inflation basis, and any policyholder behaviour assumption.
Support each with the experience analysis over the credible exposure period, showing actual versus expected and the credibility weighting applied.
Set the assumption on a best estimate basis — no implicit prudence — and state where expert judgement was used, why, and what alternatives were considered.
Take the paper to the assumptions committee and record the approval minute reference against each assumption in the assumption register.
checklist.done: every assumption is evidenced by experience analysis, set on a best estimate basis and carries an approval minute reference.

checklist.step: Apply the PRA technical information for the valuation date
actions: Download the PRA-published technical information for the valuation date: the sterling risk-free interest rate term structure with and without the volatility adjustment, and the fundamental spreads by rating and duration.
Load the curve into the model and check the loaded values against the published file at ten sample tenors, including the last liquid point and the ultimate forward rate convergence.
Record the publication date and file name of the technical information used against the model run.
Reject any run that used a prior month's curve — recalculate rather than approximate.
checklist.done: the model carries the PRA technical information for the exact valuation date, checked at ten tenors and referenced against the run.

checklist.step: Apply contract boundaries and set the cash flow projection basis
actions: Apply the contract boundary test product by product and exclude future premiums the firm can unilaterally reject or reprice to fully reflect risk.
Confirm the boundary treatment is consistent with the EPIFP calculation used in own funds — the same future premiums must be inside both.
Set the projection to include all cash in- and outflows: benefits, expenses, expense inflation, tax where relevant, and options and guarantees.
Document any events not in data allowance and its basis.
checklist.done: contract boundaries are applied product by product, consistent with the EPIFP basis, and every cash flow category is in the projection.

checklist.step: Run the best estimate liability projection and register the run
actions: Run the production model against the locked model point file and the approved assumption set on the registered model version.
Confirm the run log shows no truncated projection, no failed model point and no unconverged stochastic scenario.
Register the run in the model governance repository with the run id, model version, model point file id, assumption set id and technical information file name.
Reject and re-run rather than adjusting output where the log shows any failure.
checklist.done: a clean production run is registered with its model version, data, assumptions and curve all identified.

checklist.step: Apply the matching adjustment to eligible annuity portfolios
actions: Confirm the assigned asset portfolio and liabilities remain within the terms of the firm's matching adjustment permission and that no ineligible asset or liability has entered the portfolio since the last valuation.
Run the cash flow matching tests and record the matching quality metrics against the permission's limits.
Compute the matching adjustment spread net of the fundamental spread on the PRA published basis and apply it to the discount rate for the matching adjustment portfolio only.
Quantify the matching adjustment benefit to the best estimate and to own funds for disclosure in S.22.01 and SFCR Section D.
checklist.done: the matching adjustment is applied only to permitted portfolios, matching tests are within limits, and the benefit is quantified for disclosure.

checklist.step: Calculate the risk margin on the reformed cost-of-capital basis
actions: Project the SCR for non-hedgeable risks over the run-off of the in-force obligations using the approved risk driver proxies.
Apply the reformed 4% cost-of-capital rate together with the prescribed tapering factor, and discount the projected capital charges on the risk-free curve for the valuation date.
Allocate the resulting risk margin to lines of business for S.12.01 and S.17.01 reporting.
Show the movement from the prior valuation split into the effect of the taper, new business, run-off and risk profile change.
checklist.done: the risk margin is computed at 4% with the taper, discounted on the correct curve, allocated by line and explained against the prior period.

checklist.step: Apply and review any transitional measure on technical provisions
actions: Confirm the firm's transitional measure permission and the deduction still in force at the valuation date.
Run the amortisation of the transitional deduction over the remaining transitional period and record the amount applied.
Test the recalculation triggers — a material change in risk profile since the last recalculation — and recalculate where triggered, notifying the PRA of the recalculation.
Present the technical provisions both with and without the transitional measure, as required for reporting and disclosure.
checklist.done: the transitional deduction applied matches the permission and amortisation, recalculation triggers are tested, and figures are shown gross and net of the measure.

checklist.step: Value reinsurance recoverables and the counterparty default adjustment
actions: Project reinsurance cash flows on the same basis, timing and assumptions as the gross liabilities so gross and ceded remain consistent.
Take each reinsurer's current credit rating and compute the adjustment for expected losses due to counterparty default on the prescribed basis.
Reconcile the recoverable to the ceded balances in the ledger and to the treaty terms held in the treaty repository, particularly on any longevity swap or funded reinsurance arrangement.
Report the net technical provisions and the ceded amount separately for S.12.01.
checklist.done: recoverables are projected on the gross basis, adjusted for counterparty default, and reconciled to the ledger and treaty terms.

checklist.step: Run the movement analysis and challenge the result
actions: Build the analysis of change from the prior valuation: opening position, unwind of discount, new business, actual versus expected experience, assumption changes, model changes, economic movements, matching adjustment and transitional effects.
Confirm the walk closes to the reported best estimate with an unexplained residual below 0.25% of the opening best estimate.
Explain every step above 1% of the opening best estimate with a named driver and a supporting exhibit.
Present at the actuarial review meeting and minute the challenge, the responses and any resulting rerun.
checklist.done: the analysis of change closes to the reported figure with a residual under 0.25% and every step above 1% is explained and minuted.

checklist.step: Reconcile results into the reporting templates
actions: Hand over the signed results pack showing best estimate, risk margin, matching adjustment benefit, transitional deduction and reinsurance recoverable by homogeneous risk group.
Tie the pack to S.12.01 line by line and to the technical provisions line in S.02.01 in the reporting engine.
Confirm the run id quoted in the reporting engine matches the registered production run — no unregistered run may enter the return.
Sign the handoff sheet jointly with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: S.12.01 and S.02.01 tie to a signed results pack from a registered run, on a jointly signed handoff sheet.

checklist.step: Log limitations and manual adjustments before release
actions: Log every data limitation, model limitation and expert judgement applied at this valuation date with its quantified effect on the best estimate.
Log every manual adjustment made outside the model with the reason, the amount and the person who approved it.
Reject any manual adjustment with no quantification or no named approver — it must be modelled or removed.
Present the log to the Chief Actuary for disposition before results are released.
checklist.done: every limitation and manual adjustment is quantified, approved and dispositioned by the Chief Actuary before release.

checklist.step: Sign and file the valuation report
actions: Write the valuation report covering data, assumptions, methodology, results by homogeneous risk group, the analysis of change, limitations and the technical information used.
State compliance with the applicable technical actuarial standards and identify the expert judgements that most affect the result.
Sign and date the report and file it in the model governance repository against the valuation date.
Release the results to reporting and to the Chief Financial Officer with the report attached.
checklist.done: a signed, dated valuation report covering data, assumptions, method, results, change and limitations is filed against the valuation date.

testing.step: Build the population of valued business and rebuild the in-force independently
actions: Take your own extract of in-force policies at the valuation date directly from the administration system, using your own query rather than the actuarial extract.
Compare policy count, annuity in payment and sum assured to the valuation extract by homogeneous risk group.
Any difference above the 0.1% tolerance is an exception before any recalculation begins.
Sign the population with both extract timestamps recorded.
testing.done: an independent in-force extract reconciles to the valuation extract within 0.1% by risk group, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Reconcile the reported technical provisions to the registered model run
actions: Take the run id quoted on the handoff sheet and open the run register entry.
Confirm the model version, model point file id, assumption set id and PRA technical information file recorded against the run.
Compare the run output totals to the figures reported in S.12.01 and S.02.01 and explain any difference as a logged manual adjustment or an exception.
Confirm the run date precedes the sign-off date on the valuation report.
testing.done: the reported technical provisions trace to one registered run whose inputs are identified and whose date precedes sign-off.

testing.step: Draw the recalculation sample and document it
actions: Take 100% of homogeneous risk groups holding more than 10% of the total best estimate.
Select 200 individual model points at random using a recorded seed across the remaining groups, weighted to matching adjustment business.
Record the seed, population size and draw date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every risk group with a prior-period exception as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers every material risk group and includes all prior-period exception groups.

testing.step: Recalculate the best estimate independently on the sample
actions: Rebuild the cash flow projection for the 200 sampled model points in an independent tool using the approved assumptions and the PRA curve for the valuation date.
Compare the independent present value to the model output per model point and per risk group against the 0.5% tolerance.
Investigate every breach to the specific driver — wrong curve tenor, contract boundary treatment, expense inflation, mortality table version.
Record the recalculation workbook with its inputs in the validation file.
testing.done: the independent recalculation agrees within 0.5% by risk group or the causing driver is identified for every breach.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk margin calculation and its taper
actions: Rebuild the non-hedgeable SCR run-off projection from the risk drivers and recompute the risk margin at the 4% cost-of-capital rate with the prescribed tapering factor.
Compare to the reported risk margin against the 1% tolerance and reconcile any difference to the projection basis rather than to the rate.
Recompute the discounting on the published risk-free curve for the valuation date and confirm the correct curve was used.
Test the allocation to lines of business sums to the total reported in S.12.01 and S.17.01.
testing.done: the risk margin re-derives within 1% on the 4% and taper basis, discounted on the correct curve, and the allocation sums to the reported total.

testing.step: Verify the PRA technical information actually loaded into the model
actions: Download the PRA technical information for the valuation date yourself and compare the risk-free curve to the model input file at 15 tenors including the last liquid point.
Compare the fundamental spreads used in the matching adjustment calculation to the published values by rating and duration.
Confirm the publication date on the file used matches the valuation date rather than a prior month.
Any curve difference is an exception regardless of its effect size, because it invalidates the whole run.
testing.done: the loaded curve and fundamental spreads match the PRA publication for the valuation date at every tested point.

testing.step: Challenge the assumptions against experience independently
actions: Rerun the actual-versus-expected analysis for mortality, longevity improvement, lapse and expense over the credible exposure period from source experience data.
Reach your own view on each assumption before reading the assumption paper's conclusion.
Compare to the approved assumption and treat any assumption set outside your credible range, or set without an approval minute, as an exception.
Test that no implicit margin has been built into a best estimate assumption.
testing.done: each material assumption has an independent experience-based view, an approval minute and no implicit prudence.

testing.step: Test the matching adjustment and transitional applications
actions: Read the firm's matching adjustment permission and confirm every asset and liability in the portfolio at the valuation date is within its terms.
Re-run the cash flow matching tests and compare the matching quality metrics to the permission limits.
Recompute the transitional deduction amortisation and confirm the recalculation triggers were tested and any recalculation was notified to the PRA.
Recompute the technical provisions both with and without the transitional measure and compare to the reported presentation.
testing.done: the matching adjustment portfolio is within permission and matching limits, and the transitional deduction and its dual presentation re-derive.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, quantified effect and owner
actions: Raise one record per exception naming the risk group, the figure affected and the effect on the best estimate and on own funds in pounds.
Assign a root cause — data reconciliation, contract boundary, curve loading, assumption approval, unlogged manual adjustment, matching adjustment eligibility — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next valuation date and require a rerun where the effect exceeds the reporting materiality threshold.
Carry every open exception into the next valuation's validation as a mandatory row.
testing.done: every exception is quantified in pounds, root-caused, owned and dated before the next valuation, with reruns required above materiality.

testing.step: Issue the validation opinion with independent sign-off
actions: Compute the aggregate effect of exceptions on the best estimate, the risk margin and the SCR coverage ratio.
State the validation conclusion — fit for reporting / fit with exceptions / not fit — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who set no assumption, coded no model and ran no production run for this valuation, sign and date the opinion.
Report the opinion to the Chief Actuary, the Audit Committee and the Model Governance Committee, and file it against the valuation date.
testing.done: a signed validation opinion states the conclusion and aggregate exception effect and has been reported to the Chief Actuary and the Audit Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Chief Actuary (SIMF20) heading the actuarial function; personally signs the annual Actuarial Function Report to the board on the reliability and adequacy of technical provisions, together with the opinions on underwriting policy and on the adequacy of reinsurance arrangements

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 6, which requires the actuarial function to coordinate the calculation of technical provisions, ensure the appropriateness of methodologies, models and assumptions, assess the sufficiency and quality of data, compare best estimates against experience, and produce a written report to the board at least annually; read with the FRC Technical Actuarial Standards TAS 100 and TAS 200 that govern how the report is written

In-scope processes.value: Annual production of the Actuarial Function Report for the UK life and annuity entity: methodology and assumption appropriateness review → data sufficiency and quality assessment → back-testing of best estimates against emerging experience → opinion on the overall underwriting policy → opinion on the adequacy of reinsurance arrangements → board presentation and sign-off

In-scope systems.value: Valuation reports, model validation opinions, experience studies and the signed Actuarial Function Report are held against the reference date; the board version is distributed through the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Actuarial Function Report Standard — the mandatory content map against Conditions Governing Business 6, the evidence required behind each opinion, the back-testing method, the escalation route for a qualified opinion and the review path through the Model Risk Manager

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board on the recommendation of the Risk Committee; reviewed annually and whenever the PRA changes the actuarial function requirements or the firm changes its Chief Actuary

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — the report must reach the board before the SFCR is approved, so it is scheduled to be signed within 10 weeks of the 31 December reference date, ahead of the 14-week SFCR deadline and the 70 business day annual return deadline; the underwriting and reinsurance opinions follow the same annual cycle

Deadline reminders configured.value: Actuarial calendar tasks alert at reference date plus 4 weeks (experience studies complete), plus 7 weeks (draft report to Risk Committee) and plus 9 weeks (final report to board pack deadline); a slipped gate escalates to the Chief Risk Officer weekly

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed report, experience studies, back-testing workbooks, methodology appropriateness assessments, the underwriting and reinsurance opinion evidence packs and the board minute retained 10 years from the reference date in the model governance repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every deficiency the report identifies — data insufficiency, model limitation, assumption not supported by experience, underwriting policy inconsistent with pricing, reinsurance cover inadequate for the risk profile — is logged with severity, owner and remediation date, and tracked to closure

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Risk Officer signs off remediation of every deficiency raised in the report; the board records acceptance of any deficiency it chooses not to remediate and the reason

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The Actuarial Function Report for the reference date, every opinion and conclusion it contains, and the underlying evidence: experience studies, back-testing results, data quality reports, methodology assessments and the underwriting and reinsurance evidence packs

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every mandatory element of Conditions Governing Business 6 must be present — coordination of technical provisions, methodology and assumption appropriateness, data sufficiency and quality, comparison against experience, underwriting policy opinion, reinsurance adequacy opinion. A missing element is a fail. Any opinion with no traceable evidence pack is a fail. Back-testing showing actual outside the expected range for two consecutive years without an assumption change is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The report is annual, so the verification runs once per year on the signed report before it goes to the board, with an interim design check on the evidence packs at the half year

Evidence location for test results.value: Actuarial Function Report verification workpaper in the compliance evidence repository — the requirement map, evidence trace, back-testing re-performance, exception log and the conclusion memo — indexed by reference date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed report, the evidence packs behind each opinion and the board minute recording receipt, producible within 5 business days for a PRA actuarial deep-dive, an SIMF20 accountability review or a skilled person review

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Actuary responds to PRA questions on the report directly, coordinated through the Regulatory Reporting Manager; a qualified opinion on technical provisions is notified to the PRA supervisory contact by the Chief Risk Officer before the SFCR is published

checklist.step: Set the report scope against Conditions Governing Business 6
actions: Build the content map listing each required element of Conditions Governing Business 6 as a report section: coordination of technical provisions, appropriateness of methodologies, models and assumptions, sufficiency and quality of data, comparison of best estimates against experience, opinion on overall underwriting policy, opinion on adequacy of reinsurance arrangements, contribution to risk management.
Name the evidence pack that will support each section and its owner within the actuarial function.
Confirm the entity and business scope covered — every UK legal entity and every line the actuarial function serves.
Circulate the map to the Model Risk Manager and the Chief Risk Officer for challenge before drafting starts.
checklist.done: a content map covers every rulebook element with a named evidence pack and owner, challenged by second line.

checklist.step: Evidence the coordination of the technical provisions calculation
actions: Assemble the quarterly and annual valuation reports for the reference year with their registered run ids and sign-off dates.
Show how the actuarial function directed the calculation: assumption approvals, methodology decisions, model change approvals and results challenge minutes.
Confirm the technical provisions reported in S.12.01 and S.02.01 came from runs the actuarial function registered and signed.
Record any occasion where reported figures differed from actuarial output and how it was resolved.
checklist.done: the pack evidences actuarial direction of every valuation in the year and ties reported figures to signed actuarial runs.

checklist.step: Assess the appropriateness of methodologies, models and assumptions
actions: Take the model inventory for technical provisions and record each model's validation status, last validation date and open validation findings.
Assess each methodology against the nature, scale and complexity of the risks — proportionality is a conclusion to be evidenced, not asserted.
List every material expert judgement, its rationale, the alternatives considered and its sensitivity on the best estimate.
State clearly where a methodology is judged not appropriate and what will change.
checklist.done: every model has a validation status and every material expert judgement has a rationale and a quantified sensitivity.

checklist.step: Assess the sufficiency and quality of the data used
actions: Consolidate the data quality reports for each valuation date in the year against the completeness, accuracy and appropriateness criteria.
List every unresolved data deficiency, the proxy or approximation used in its place and the quantified effect on the best estimate.
Assess whether the data is sufficient for the methodology chosen — insufficient data with a sophisticated model is a finding, not a neutral fact.
Recommend the data improvements needed and name the system owner who must deliver them.
checklist.done: data sufficiency is concluded on with every deficiency quantified and a named owner for each recommended improvement.

checklist.step: Back-test best estimates against emerging experience
actions: For mortality, longevity, lapse, expense and claims experience, compare the actual outcome in the year to the best estimate assumption applied at the start of it.
Express each as an actual-to-expected ratio with a confidence range reflecting the exposure, and chart the ratio over at least five years.
Flag any assumption where actual sits outside the expected range for two consecutive years and state whether the assumption was changed and why.
Conclude on whether the best estimates have been systematically optimistic or prudent.
checklist.done: every material assumption has a multi-year actual-to-expected series and a stated conclusion on systematic bias.

checklist.step: Form the opinion on the overall underwriting policy
actions: Read the current underwriting policy and the pricing bases in force for the products written in the year.
Test whether premiums written are sufficient to cover expected claims, expenses and the cost of capital, using the actual new business mix.
Assess anti-selection risk, medical underwriting standards, guarantee terms and the effect of any pricing discretion actually exercised in the year.
Write the opinion with the evidence behind it, and state plainly where the policy is not adequate for a named product.
checklist.done: a written underwriting policy opinion exists, tested against the actual new business mix, naming any inadequate product.

checklist.step: Form the opinion on the adequacy of reinsurance arrangements
actions: List the treaties in force at the reference date with retentions, limits, exclusions, and the counterparty and its rating.
Test the cover against the firm's risk profile and stress scenarios — concentration by scheme, longevity exposure ceded, funded reinsurance collateral arrangements and recapture triggers.
Assess counterparty credit concentration and the effect of a single reinsurer default on own funds and the SCR.
Write the opinion stating whether the programme is adequate and naming any gap, unpriced exclusion or excessive concentration.
checklist.done: a written reinsurance opinion tests cover against the risk profile and stresses and names every gap or concentration.

checklist.step: Evidence the actuarial function's contribution to risk management
actions: Record the actuarial function's contribution to the ORSA: the stress and scenario work, the projection of the solvency position and the risk appetite calibration.
Record its contribution to the SCR calculation and to the asset-liability management framework.
Attach the meeting minutes and deliverables that prove the contribution rather than asserting it.
Note any occasion where actuarial advice was not followed and what happened.
checklist.done: the contribution to ORSA, SCR and ALM is evidenced by dated deliverables, including any advice not followed.

checklist.step: Draft the report to the technical actuarial standards
actions: Draft each section against the content map, stating the purpose, the scope, the users and the material judgements as the technical actuarial standards require.
Make each conclusion explicit and traceable — every opinion sentence carries a reference to its evidence pack.
State every material limitation and uncertainty clearly enough that a non-actuarial board member can act on it.
Write a plain-language executive summary that leads with the deficiencies, not the reassurances.
checklist.done: the draft covers every mapped section, each opinion cites its evidence pack, and the summary leads with deficiencies.

checklist.step: Put the draft through independent actuarial review
actions: Review the draft against the content map and the rulebook text, marking any required element that is present in name but not substantiated.
Challenge every conclusion where the evidence supports a weaker statement than the one written.
Record the review points and the Chief Actuary's responses in a challenge log attached to the report.
Confirm no review point was closed by deletion of the underlying issue rather than by resolution.
checklist.done: an independent review challenge log is attached with a response to every point, none closed by deletion.

checklist.step: Take the report to the Risk Committee
actions: Table the draft report, the challenge log and the deficiency list at the Risk Committee at reference date plus seven weeks.
Focus the discussion on the deficiencies and on the two opinions, not on the technical provisions numbers themselves.
Record the committee's challenge and any request for further work in the minutes.
Confirm the committee is content for the report to go to the board, or set the conditions for it to do so.
checklist.done: the Risk Committee has challenged the report and its minute states whether it may proceed to the board and on what conditions.

checklist.step: Sign the report and present it to the board
actions: Sign and date the final report in the SIMF20 capacity and load it to the board portal with the deficiency list.
Present the conclusions to the board in person, taking questions on the two opinions and on any qualification.
Ask the board to record receipt of the report and its decision on each deficiency — remediate or accept with reasons.
Confirm the minute names the report version received.
checklist.done: the board has received a signed, version-identified report and minuted a decision on every deficiency.

checklist.step: Escalate a qualified opinion outside the normal cycle
actions: Where the report qualifies the reliability or adequacy of technical provisions, notify the board chair and the Audit Committee chair within one business day of the qualification being settled.
Assess notification to the PRA under Fundamental Rule 7 and prepare the notification with the qualification wording and its quantified effect.
Ensure the SFCR Section D narrative and the Regulatory Reporting Manager both reflect the qualification before submission.
Record the assessment and its outcome even where no notification is made.
checklist.done: any qualification is escalated within one business day, assessed for PRA notification and reflected in the SFCR before submission.

checklist.step: Track the report's deficiencies to closure
actions: Open one record per deficiency with the report section, the severity, the owner and a remediation date before the next reference date.
Link each to the underlying model validation finding or data issue so the same problem is not tracked twice.
Report ageing to the Risk Committee quarterly.
Require the next year's report to state explicitly what happened to each prior-year deficiency.
checklist.done: every deficiency is tracked with an owner and a date before the next reference date, and the next report must revisit each one.

checklist.step: File the report and its evidence for retention
actions: File the signed report, the challenge log, the deficiency list, all evidence packs and the board minute against the reference date.
Index by reference date, entity and report section so a single opinion and its evidence can be produced alone.
Apply the 10-year retention label and lock the file against edit after the board date.
Test retrieval of the prior year's reinsurance opinion pack to prove the index works.
checklist.done: the report file is complete, indexed by section, locked, labelled for 10 years and retrieval-tested.

testing.step: Build the requirement map and test the report for completeness
actions: Write out each element required by PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 6 from the rulebook text, not from the firm's content map.
Tick each element against the signed report, recording the page and paragraph that satisfies it.
Treat an element present only as a heading with no conclusion as missing.
Sign the completeness assessment naming the rulebook snapshot date used.
testing.done: every rulebook element is traced to a substantive conclusion in the report, with missing elements listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the report's technical provisions figures to the filed returns
actions: Take every technical provisions figure quoted in the report and compare it to the submitted S.12.01 and S.02.01 for the reference date.
Confirm the run ids the report relies on match the runs registered against those submissions.
Any figure in the report that does not appear in the filed return is an exception — the board must not be told a different number from the regulator.
Record the comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: every technical provisions figure in the report matches the filed return and traces to the same registered run.

testing.step: Sample the opinions and trace each to its evidence pack
actions: Take 100% of the two mandatory opinions and 12 further conclusions selected at random with a recorded seed.
For each, open the cited evidence pack and confirm it exists, is dated before the report signature and supports the strength of the wording used.
Downgrade any conclusion where the evidence supports a weaker statement than the report makes, and record it as an exception.
Record the seed, population and draw date.
testing.done: both mandatory opinions and the 12 sampled conclusions trace to dated evidence that supports the wording used.

testing.step: Re-perform the back-testing of best estimates against experience
actions: Take the year's actual mortality, longevity, lapse and expense experience from source and recompute the actual-to-expected ratios against the opening assumptions.
Compare your ratios to those in the report and reconcile any difference to the exposure basis used.
Identify any assumption outside the expected range for two consecutive years and confirm the report says so and explains the response.
Flag a report that presents only favourable experience series.
testing.done: the actual-to-expected ratios re-derive, and every two-year breach is disclosed and explained in the report.

testing.step: Test the underwriting policy opinion against actual new business
actions: Take the actual new business written in the year by product and compare the achieved premium to the pricing basis.
Recompute whether premiums cover expected claims, expenses and cost of capital on the actual mix rather than the planned mix.
Test whether pricing discretion exercised in the year was within the underwriting policy limits.
Any product where the recomputed margin is negative and the opinion is silent is an exception.
testing.done: the underwriting opinion is tested on the actual new business mix, with every negative-margin product either disclosed or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Test the reinsurance adequacy opinion against the treaties in force
actions: Pull the treaty schedule at the reference date and compare retentions, limits, exclusions and counterparties to those described in the opinion.
Confirm any treaty incepted or lapsed during the year is reflected, including funded reinsurance and longevity swap arrangements.
Re-perform the single-reinsurer default stress and compare the effect on own funds to the figure quoted in the opinion.
Flag any exclusion or recapture trigger the opinion does not mention.
testing.done: the opinion's treaty description matches the schedule and the default stress effect re-derives, with unmentioned exclusions flagged.

testing.step: Test data sufficiency conclusions against the data quality reports
actions: Take the data quality reports for each valuation date and list every unresolved deficiency and its quantified effect.
Compare that list to the deficiencies disclosed in the report.
Any material unresolved deficiency omitted from the report is an exception.
Confirm each recommended data improvement names a system owner and a date.
testing.done: every material unresolved data deficiency appears in the report with its quantified effect and a named improvement owner.

testing.step: Verify the governance path, signature and board receipt
actions: Confirm the report was reviewed independently, that the challenge log holds a response to every point, and that no point was closed by deleting the issue.
Confirm the signature is that of the SIMF20 holder and is dated before the board meeting and before the SFCR approval.
Open the board minute and confirm it records receipt of the named report version and a decision on each deficiency.
Confirm any qualification was escalated within one business day and assessed for PRA notification.
testing.done: the report is independently reviewed, signed by the SIMF20 holder before board and SFCR approval, and receipt with per-deficiency decisions is minuted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one record per exception naming the report section, the missing element or unsupported conclusion and the governance exposure it creates.
Assign a root cause — element omitted, evidence not retained, conclusion stronger than evidence, experience series filtered, timing after SFCR approval — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next reference date so the next report cannot repeat it.
Carry every open exception into next year's verification as a mandatory row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, owner and a remediation date before the next report is produced.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the count of missing rulebook elements and unsupported conclusions against the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion — compliant / compliant with exceptions / non-compliant — with workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside the actuarial function and contributed to no opinion, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Risk Committee before the SFCR is approved and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception count and has been reported to both committees before SFCR approval.
