checklist.step: Confirm the annual submission scope with the PRA supervisory contact
actions: Write to the named PRA supervisory contact before the reference date confirming which actuarial deliverables the supervisor expects with the annual package this year.
Confirm whether the actuarial function report is to be submitted proactively or held available on request, and record the answer in the submission scope note.
Confirm the matching adjustment attestation scope and its expected submission route.
File the correspondence — the scope note is the defence if a deliverable is later said to be missing.
checklist.done: a written scope confirmation from the supervisor is on file naming every actuarial deliverable expected for the reference date.

checklist.step: Register the BEEDS return codes and the authorised submitters
actions: Log in to the Bank of England BEEDS portal against the firm's Firm Reference Number and list the returns open for the reference date.
Confirm the return codes and reporting periods match the firm's obligations under PS15/24 and record them in the submission scope note.
Reconcile the BEEDS user list to the authorised submitter list and remove anyone who has changed role or left.
Confirm at least two authorised submitters are active so a single absence cannot stop a filing.
checklist.done: the open returns, codes and periods are confirmed in BEEDS and the submitter list is reconciled with at least two active users.

checklist.step: Take handover of the signed actuarial function report
actions: Receive the signed report from the Chief Actuary with the handover checklist: reference date, signature date, SIMF20 signatory, version identifier and the board minute reference for receipt.
Compute and record the file hash of the received document so the submitted file can later be proved identical.
Refuse handover of an unsigned draft, a document with tracked changes, or a version not matching the board minute.
Store the received file read-only in the submission folder for the reference date.
checklist.done: a signed, version-identified report is received with its hash recorded and stored read-only.

checklist.step: Take handover of the matching adjustment attestation
actions: Receive the attestation signed by the accountable senior manager confirming that the fundamental spread reflects all retained risks in the matching adjustment portfolio.
Check it names the portfolios covered, the reference date and the evidence relied on, and that the supporting analysis is attached.
Confirm the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary's underlying assessment is filed and dated before the attestation signature.
Record the attestation in the submission scope note as a separate deliverable with its own due date.
checklist.done: a signed attestation naming portfolios, reference date and evidence is held with its supporting analysis dated before signature.

checklist.step: Package the annual quantitative templates with the actuarial content
actions: Generate the annual return instance carrying S.02.01, S.12.01, S.17.01, S.22.01, S.23.01, S.25.01, S.28 and the required National Specific Templates.
Confirm the technical provisions in the instance came from the run id quoted on the actuarial handover sheet.
Attach the actuarial deliverables in the format the return requires, using the naming standard so the supervisor can identify each file without opening it.
Run a pre-submission validation and clear every blocking failure.
checklist.done: the packaged instance validates clean, ties to the registered actuarial run and carries correctly named attachments.

checklist.step: Obtain internal sign-off before upload
actions: Review the submission pack summary: templates included, actuarial deliverables attached, key figures and any qualification carried in the actuarial report.
Confirm the Chief Actuary and the Controller have both signed their sections of the pre-submission sign-off sheet.
Sign the sheet and record the date and time, which must precede the upload.
Withhold sign-off where any deliverable is unsigned or any validation failure is unresolved.
checklist.done: a three-party pre-submission sign-off sheet is signed and time-stamped before any upload takes place.

checklist.step: Recompute the submission deadline before uploading
actions: Count 70 business days forward from the 31 December reference date on the England and Wales business day calendar including bank holidays.
Where a group return is also filed, count 82 business days for the group deadline.
Record the computed dates in the submission scope note alongside the 14-week SFCR date.
Target upload at least three business days before the earliest of them and escalate to the CFO if that is not achievable.
checklist.done: the deadlines are recomputed on the business day calendar and the planned upload date carries at least three business days of headroom.

checklist.step: Upload the package through BEEDS
actions: Log in to BEEDS as an authorised submitter, open the return for the reference date and upload the instance and each attachment.
Wait for the portal to complete processing and confirm the status shows accepted rather than pending or failed.
Where the portal reports a validation failure, correct and re-upload the same day — a return left failed is not submitted.
Download the submission receipt showing the return code, reference date, file names and timestamp.
checklist.done: BEEDS shows the return as accepted with every attachment present and the receipt is downloaded.

checklist.step: Prove the submitted document is the signed document
actions: Recompute the hash of the file as uploaded and compare it to the hash recorded at handover.
Compare the file names and sizes on the BEEDS receipt to the submission folder contents.
Any difference means an unsigned or edited version was submitted — escalate to the CFO immediately and resubmit.
Record the hash comparison result in the submission log.
checklist.done: the uploaded file hash matches the hash recorded at handover and the comparison is logged.

checklist.step: Archive the receipts and close the submission record
actions: File the receipt, the submitted instance, the attachments, the sign-off sheet and the deadline computation together under the reference date.
Record the actual submission timestamp and the headroom in business days in the submission log.
Apply the 10-year retention label and lock the folder against edit.
Mark the return closed in the filing calendar only after the receipt is filed.
checklist.done: the submission record is complete with receipt, headroom and retention label, and the calendar entry is closed against filed evidence.

checklist.step: Log and answer PRA follow-up requests on the actuarial content
actions: Open a tracked item the day any PRA request arrives, recording the requester, the exact question, the stated due date and the deliverable required.
Route technical questions to the Chief Actuary and evidence requests to the model governance repository owner, with an internal due date two business days before the PRA date.
Have the Chief Risk Officer clear any response that acknowledges a limitation, qualification or error before it is sent.
Send through the named supervisory contact only, and file the sent response against the tracked item.
checklist.done: every PRA request is tracked from arrival with an internal due date, cleared where sensitive, and answered through the named contact.

checklist.step: Handle resubmission when an error is found after filing
actions: Quantify the error's effect on technical provisions, own funds and the SCR coverage ratio with the Chief Actuary.
Notify the PRA supervisory contact of the error and the intended correction before uploading anything.
Obtain CFO approval, regenerate the instance and resubmit through BEEDS against the same reference date.
Record the original and corrected receipts side by side and open a root cause item for the control that let the error through.
checklist.done: any post-submission error is quantified, notified before resubmission, CFO-approved, resubmitted and root-caused.

checklist.step: Reconcile submitted actuarial figures to the SFCR and the accounts
actions: Compare the technical provisions in the submitted S.12.01 to the figures disclosed in SFCR Section D and in the actuarial function report.
Compare own funds and the SCR coverage ratio across the annual return, the SFCR and the board pack.
Any inconsistency between what the regulator, the public and the board were told is escalated to the CFO the same day.
File the three-way reconciliation with the submission record.
checklist.done: a three-way reconciliation shows the return, the SFCR and the board pack carry the same technical provisions, own funds and coverage ratio.

checklist.step: Review submitter access and segregation after the cycle
actions: Recertify every BEEDS submitter and every reporting engine approver against the current authorised list.
Remove access for leavers and role changers within five business days of the trigger and record the ticket.
Confirm no individual holds both the ability to change template output and the ability to submit it.
Report the recertification result to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: submitter access is recertified with leavers removed and no individual holding both change and submit rights.

checklist.step: Report the annual submission position to the Audit Committee
actions: Present the submission status page: deliverable, deadline, actual date, headroom in business days and receipt reference.
Report every PRA follow-up request in the year, its due date and whether it was answered on time.
Report any resubmission with its cause and the control change made.
Minute the committee's acknowledgement and any directed action.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has a minuted view of every actuarial deliverable's deadline, headroom, requests and resubmissions.

testing.step: Build the population of required and actual actuarial submissions
actions: Derive the required deliverable list independently from PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 6, the Reporting Part and the Matching Adjustment Part, plus the supervisor's written scope confirmation.
Extract from the submission log every deliverable actually submitted for the reference date with its timestamp.
Any required deliverable with no submission and no documented 'on request' basis is a critical exception before sampling.
Sign the population with both source references.
testing.done: the independently derived requirement list reconciles to the submission log, with unmatched requirements logged as critical.

testing.step: Reconcile BEEDS receipts to the submission log
actions: Log in to BEEDS as a read-only user and list the returns and attachments recorded against the reference date.
Compare the portal record to the internal submission log on return code, file names and timestamps.
Treat any return showing pending, failed or partially validated status as not submitted, whatever the internal log says.
Capture the portal listing into the workpaper.
testing.done: the portal record and the internal log agree on every return, attachment and timestamp, with any non-accepted status treated as unfiled.

testing.step: Recompute every deadline on the business day calendar
actions: Recount 70 business days from 31 December for the solo annual return and 82 for the group return using the England and Wales calendar including bank holidays.
Recount 14 weeks for the SFCR and take the stated due date for the matching adjustment attestation.
Compare each to the receipt timestamp and state the headroom or lateness in days.
Any negative headroom is a fail regardless of whether the PRA commented.
testing.done: every deadline is independently recomputed and each deliverable's headroom or lateness is stated in days.

testing.step: Prove the submitted file is the signed file
actions: Recompute the hash of the archived submitted actuarial function report and compare it to the hash recorded at handover from the Chief Actuary.
Open the document and confirm the signature, the SIMF20 signatory name and the version identifier match the board minute.
Confirm the document carries no tracked changes, comments or draft watermark.
A hash mismatch is a fail even where the content appears identical.
testing.done: the archived submitted report hashes to the handover value and matches the board-minuted version and signatory.

testing.step: Test the pre-submission sign-off and its timing
actions: Open the sign-off sheet and confirm the Chief Actuary, the Controller and the CFO all signed distinct sections.
Compare each signature timestamp to the BEEDS upload timestamp and fail any signature dated after upload.
Confirm the sheet records that all blocking validation failures were cleared before sign-off.
Confirm the person who uploaded is on the authorised submitter list as at the upload date.
testing.done: three distinct pre-upload signatures exist, all timed before upload, by an authorised submitter.

testing.step: Trace the submitted technical provisions to the registered actuarial run
actions: Take the technical provisions in the submitted S.12.01 and the run id on the actuarial handover sheet.
Open the run register and confirm the run's output matches the submitted figures by homogeneous risk group.
Confirm the run date precedes the handover and the handover precedes the upload.
Any figure not traceable to a registered run is an exception.
testing.done: the submitted technical provisions trace to a registered run whose dates sit correctly before handover and upload.

testing.step: Test the three-way consistency of what regulator, public and board were told
actions: Compare technical provisions, own funds and the SCR coverage ratio across the submitted annual return, the published SFCR and the board pack.
Compare any qualification in the actuarial function report to the wording used in SFCR Section D.
Any inconsistency is an exception, with the direction of the difference recorded.
Capture the three source extracts into the workpaper.
testing.done: the return, the SFCR and the board pack agree on technical provisions, own funds, coverage ratio and any qualification.

testing.step: Age the PRA request log and test response timeliness
actions: Extract every PRA request in the year with its arrival date, stated due date and response date.
Take 100% of requests touching technical provisions or the matching adjustment and 5 others at random.
Open the sent response and confirm it answers the question asked and was cleared by the Chief Risk Officer where it acknowledged a limitation or error.
Any response after its stated due date is a fail.
testing.done: every sampled request has a timely, on-point response with the required clearance evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one record per exception naming the deliverable, the deadline or control missed and the supervisory exposure created.
Assign a root cause — scope not confirmed, handover accepted unsigned, upload left failed, hash mismatch, submitter access stale, request untracked — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next annual cycle's equivalent gate.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory row.
testing.done: every exception has a root cause, owner and a remediation date before the next annual cycle.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance lateness and hash-identity thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who holds no BEEDS submitter access and prepared none of the submitted documents, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the reference date.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception count and has been reported to the Audit Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual liquidity plan and the cash-flow projection behind it for the UK annuity and life portfolios, including the matching adjustment portfolios, and reports the liquidity position to the Chief Risk Officer monthly

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PRA Rulebook Conditions Governing Business 3 (liquidity risk management and the requirement to maintain a liquidity plan projecting incoming and outgoing cash flows), read with Conditions Governing Business 6 (actuarial function input to asset-liability management) and Matching Adjustment 2-3 on the cash flow matching of assigned portfolios; supervisory expectations taken from the PRA's liquidity risk management statement of policy for insurers

In-scope processes.value: Annual liquidity plan production and its monthly monitoring for the UK life and annuity entity: liability cash flow projection from the valuation model → asset cash flow and monetisation profile → derivative collateral and repo margin projection → normal and stressed scenario runs → liquidity buffer sizing → contingency funding plan → board approval

In-scope systems.value: Asset cash flows, monetisation haircuts and derivative collateral positions are drawn from the investment management platform; liability cash flows come from the actuarial modelling platform and the combined projection is held with the plan in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Liquidity Risk Management and Liquidity Plan Procedure — the cash flow projection method by horizon (5 day, 1 month, 3 month, 1 year, run-off), the stress scenario library, the monetisation haircut table, buffer sizing rules, early warning indicators and the contingency funding plan invocation steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board on the recommendation of the Risk Committee as part of the liquidity risk appetite; reviewed annually and after any invocation of the contingency funding plan or any material change to the derivative or repo programme

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The liquidity plan is approved annually alongside the ORSA and before the SFCR is finalised, so it is scheduled for board approval within 12 weeks of the 31 December reference date; the projection is refreshed monthly by the fifth business day and the stress suite is re-run quarterly and immediately on a market event

Deadline reminders configured.value: Monthly monitoring tasks alert the Treasury Analyst on the third business day; the annual plan calendar alerts at reference date plus 6 and plus 10 weeks; early warning indicator breaches trigger an immediate alert to the Chief Risk Officer regardless of the calendar

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Liquidity plan, cash flow projections by horizon, stress scenario results, buffer composition and haircut evidence, collateral call history, early warning indicator dashboards and the board approval minute retained 10 years from the plan date in the model governance repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every breach of a liquidity early warning indicator or limit, every buffer shortfall under a stress scenario, and every occasion a collateral call was met by an asset outside the approved buffer, is logged with the horizon affected, the cause and a remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Risk Officer signs off remediation of every limit breach and buffer shortfall; the board approves any change to liquidity risk appetite arising from it

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The approved liquidity plan for the reference date, the twelve monthly cash flow projections in the year, every stress scenario run, the buffer composition at each month end, and the full population of derivative collateral and repo margin calls settled during the year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Projected net cash flow must remain positive at every horizon under the severe-but-plausible stress with the buffer applied; a projected shortfall at any horizon is a fail. Buffer assets must meet the monetisation criteria after haircut, and any buffer asset that could not be monetised within its stated horizon is a fail. Liability cash flows must reconcile to the valuation model run within 1%

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The plan is annual but the projection is monthly and the stresses quarterly, so verification runs annually in full over the approved plan and quarterly on a reduced scope covering the projection reconciliation, the buffer composition and the collateral call history

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Second-line risk reviews the plan and its projections; the reviewer must not sit in Treasury or Investments and must not have set a haircut or a scenario used in the plan

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual liquidity plan validation file in the model governance repository — projection reconciliation, independent stress re-performance, buffer monetisation testing, collateral call sample and the conclusion memo — with a copy of the conclusion in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved liquidity plan, projections by horizon, stress results, buffer composition with haircuts and the contingency funding plan producible within 5 business days for a PRA liquidity review, a matching adjustment review or a skilled person review

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer owns PRA liquidity correspondence through the supervisory contact; a projected or actual buffer shortfall, or an invocation of the contingency funding plan, is notified to the PRA under Fundamental Rule 7 without waiting for the next scheduled report

checklist.step: Set the liquidity risk appetite and the horizons the plan must cover
actions: Define the survival horizons the plan projects — 5 business days, 1 month, 3 months, 1 year and full run-off — and the minimum net cash flow required at each under stress.
Set the early warning indicators and their trigger levels: buffer coverage ratio, collateral call size versus buffer, concentration in a single monetisation route, and time to monetise.
Confirm the appetite is consistent with the matching adjustment portfolios' constraint that assigned assets cannot be freely sold.
Take the appetite to the board with the plan and record the approval minute reference in the plan header.
checklist.done: the plan carries board-approved horizons, minimum net cash flow levels and early warning indicator triggers, with a minute reference.

checklist.step: Project the liability cash outflows from the valuation model
actions: Take the best estimate cash flows from the registered valuation run at the reference date, split by annuity payments, death and surrender benefits, expenses and tax.
Convert the annual projection into monthly buckets for the first year and quarterly to year five so short-horizon liquidity is visible.
Reconcile the total projected outflow to the best estimate liability in S.12.01 within 1% and record the reconciliation.
Separate the cash flows arising inside the matching adjustment portfolios from those outside them.
checklist.done: monthly and quarterly liability outflows reconcile to the registered valuation run within 1% and are split by matching adjustment portfolio.

checklist.step: Project the asset cash inflows and the monetisation profile
actions: Extract contractual asset cash flows at the reference date: coupons, redemptions, scheduled amortisation on private credit and equity release mortgage cash flows.
For each holding, record the monetisation route (maturity, sale, repo) and the realistic time to cash under normal and stressed market conditions.
Apply the approved haircut table by asset class and rating and evidence each haircut against observed market depth or a documented judgement.
Mark assets assigned to a matching adjustment portfolio as unavailable for general monetisation and exclude them from the buffer.
checklist.done: asset inflows, monetisation routes, times to cash and haircuts are recorded per holding, with matching adjustment assets excluded from the buffer.

checklist.step: Project derivative collateral and repo margin flows
actions: List every derivative and repo position with its counterparty, CSA terms, eligible collateral, thresholds and minimum transfer amounts.
Project variation margin calls under the interest rate, inflation and credit spread moves in the stress library, including same-day sterling cash calls.
Test whether eligible collateral would be available in the required form and within the settlement deadline, not merely on the balance sheet.
Record the largest single-day projected call and compare it to the buffer's same-day cash capacity.
checklist.done: projected margin calls by scenario are quantified, tested against eligible collateral form and timing, and the largest one-day call is compared to same-day capacity.

checklist.step: Build the base case net cash flow projection by horizon
actions: Combine liability outflows, asset inflows, premium and reinsurance flows, expenses, tax and dividend payments into a single net projection at each horizon.
Include reinsurance recoveries only on their contractual settlement timing, not on the date the claim is paid.
Show the opening cash and buffer position and the running balance at every horizon.
Have the Chief Investment Officer confirm the asset side and the Appointed Actuary confirm the liability side before the projection is used.
checklist.done: a single base case projection shows the running position at every horizon, confirmed by both the asset and liability owners.

checklist.step: Run the stressed scenarios required by the plan
actions: Run the scenario library: a sharp rise in gilt yields driving collateral calls, a credit spread widening reducing monetisation value, a mass lapse on unit-linked and surrenderable business, a reinsurer default, and an operational payment system outage.
Run a combined severe-but-plausible scenario rather than only single-factor stresses, and state the correlation assumptions used.
For each scenario record the net position at each horizon and the point of first shortfall if any.
Include a reverse stress test identifying the market move that would exhaust the buffer at the 1 month horizon.
checklist.done: every scenario, the combined stress and a reverse stress test are run with the net position and first shortfall point recorded per horizon.

checklist.step: Size and compose the liquidity buffer
actions: Size the buffer to cover the worst stressed net outflow at each horizon with the board-approved margin.

Compose it from assets that are unencumbered, not assigned to a matching adjustment portfolio, and monetisable within the horizon after haircut — cash, short gilts and repo-eligible high quality collateral.
Record the concentration of the buffer by asset, counterparty and monetisation route and test it against the concentration trigger.
Report the buffer coverage ratio per horizon monthly to the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: the buffer covers the worst stressed outflow at every horizon from unencumbered, monetisable, non-matching-adjustment assets within concentration limits.

checklist.step: Write the contingency funding plan and its invocation triggers
actions: Set the quantitative triggers that invoke the plan — buffer coverage below the board minimum, a single-day margin call above a stated size, loss of a repo counterparty.
Name the actions in priority order with the cash each raises and the time it takes: draw committed facilities, repo gilts, sell listed assets, suspend dividends, request intragroup support.
Name the invocation authority, the escalation path and the communication plan to the board, the PRA and rating agencies.
Test the availability of every committed facility against its current terms, covenants and expiry date.
checklist.done: the plan states quantitative triggers, prioritised actions with amounts and timings, named authorities and tested facility availability.

checklist.step: Test matching adjustment portfolio liquidity separately
actions: Confirm each matching adjustment portfolio is self-sufficient for its own annuity outflows without recourse to the general buffer.
Re-run the cash flow matching tests under stress and check the matching quality metrics stay within the permission's limits.
Test the effect of asset restructuring or a downgrade forcing a sale within the portfolio, including the fundamental spread and matching adjustment benefit consequences.
Report any portfolio that would need general buffer support to the Chief Risk Officer as a permission risk, not only a liquidity risk.
checklist.done: each matching adjustment portfolio is shown self-sufficient under stress within its matching limits, with any exception escalated as a permission risk.

checklist.step: Monitor the position monthly and act on early warning indicators
actions: Refresh the projection by the fifth business day each month with actual cash flows for the prior month and updated positions.
Publish the dashboard: buffer coverage ratio by horizon, largest single-day collateral call in the month, concentration measures and time-to-monetise.
Compare actual cash flows against the prior month's projection and explain every variance above 10% of the projected net flow.
Escalate any indicator breach to the Chief Risk Officer on the day it is observed rather than in the monthly pack.
checklist.done: the dashboard is published by the fifth business day with variance explanations above 10% and same-day escalation of any breach.

checklist.step: Run a live monetisation test at least annually
actions: Select a representative buffer asset and execute an actual sale or repo to prove the monetisation route works end to end with the counterparty and the custodian.
Record the time from decision to cash received and compare it to the assumed time to monetise in the plan.
Compare the realised price to the haircut assumed and revise the haircut table where the test shows it optimistic.
Repeat with a private credit or illiquid holding to test the more difficult route.
checklist.done: a live monetisation test has been executed on both a liquid and an illiquid holding with realised timings and prices compared to the assumptions.

checklist.step: Integrate the plan with the ORSA and the SFCR narrative
actions: Feed the stressed liquidity results into the ORSA's forward-looking assessment and confirm the ORSA and the plan use the same scenarios and severities.
Draft the liquidity risk paragraphs of SFCR Section C from the plan so the public disclosure and the internal plan cannot diverge.
Confirm the actuarial function's contribution to asset-liability management is evidenced in both documents.
Cross-reference the plan version in the ORSA and the SFCR.
checklist.done: the ORSA and SFCR Section C draw on the same scenario set and cite the plan version, with the actuarial contribution evidenced.

checklist.step: Take the liquidity plan to the board for approval
actions: Load the plan, the stress results, the buffer composition and the contingency funding plan to the board portal within 12 weeks of the reference date.
Present the worst-case horizon, the reverse stress result and any indicator breach in the year.
Ask the board to approve the plan and the liquidity risk appetite and to record any action it directs.
Minute the approval with the plan version identifier.
checklist.done: the board has approved a version-identified plan and appetite, with the reverse stress and any breaches minuted.

checklist.step: Log and remediate every limit breach and shortfall
actions: Open a record for each early warning indicator breach, projected buffer shortfall or collateral call met from outside the buffer, naming the horizon and the cause.
Assign an owner and a remediation action — rebalance the buffer, add a committed facility, revise a haircut, reduce a concentration.
Assess whether the breach requires PRA notification under Fundamental Rule 7 and record the assessment either way.
Report open items and ageing to the Risk Committee monthly.
checklist.done: every breach and shortfall is logged with cause, owner, action, a notification assessment and monthly Risk Committee reporting.

checklist.step: File the plan and its supporting projections for retention
actions: File the approved plan, all projections by horizon, the stress results, the haircut evidence, the monetisation test results and the board minute against the plan date.
Index by reference date, horizon and scenario so a single stress result can be produced on its own.
Apply the 10-year retention label and lock the file after board approval.
Test retrieval of the prior year's severe-but-plausible scenario result to prove the index works.
checklist.done: the plan file is complete, indexed by scenario and horizon, locked, labelled for 10 years and retrieval-tested.

testing.step: Build the population of projections, scenarios and collateral calls
actions: List the twelve monthly projections, every stress run and every quarterly buffer composition for the year from the model governance repository.
Extract the full population of derivative variation margin and repo margin calls settled in the year from the treasury and custodian records.
Compare the scenario list actually run to the board-approved scenario library and treat any unrun scenario as a critical exception.
Sign the population with the repository and treasury extract dates.
testing.done: the population covers all projections, scenarios and settled margin calls, with any unrun approved scenario logged as critical.

testing.step: Reconcile the projected liability outflows to the valuation model
actions: Take the registered valuation run for the reference date and extract its best estimate cash flows independently.
Rebuild the monthly and quarterly buckets and compare the total to the plan's liability outflow against the 1% tolerance.
Confirm the matching adjustment portfolio split in the plan matches the portfolio definitions in the permission.
Any bucketing that shifts outflows into later horizons without a stated basis is an exception.
testing.done: the plan's liability outflows re-derive from the registered run within 1% with the matching adjustment split matching the permission.

testing.step: Draw the sample of holdings, scenarios and margin calls
actions: Take 100% of buffer holdings and 100% of stress scenarios showing a shortfall at any horizon.
Select 30 non-buffer holdings and 25 settled margin calls at random using a recorded seed, weighted to the largest calls.
Record the seed, population size and draw date so the sample can be redrawn.
Add every prior-year exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers every buffer holding and shortfall scenario, is reproducible, and includes prior-year exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the stress projections independently
actions: Rebuild the severe-but-plausible combined scenario in an independent workbook using the board-approved severities and the same starting positions.
Recompute the net position at the 5 day, 1 month, 3 month and 1 year horizons and compare to the plan's figures.
Test the correlation assumptions used to combine stresses — a combined stress softer than the sum of its parts must be justified.
Confirm the reverse stress test genuinely exhausts the buffer rather than stopping at a comfortable point.
testing.done: the combined stress net position re-derives at every horizon with justified correlations and a genuine reverse stress result.

testing.step: Test buffer eligibility, encumbrance and haircuts
actions: For every buffer holding, confirm from the custodian record that it is unencumbered and not pledged as collateral or assigned to a matching adjustment portfolio.
Compare each applied haircut to observable market evidence at the reference date and to the realised price in the live monetisation test.
Recompute the buffer value after haircut and compare it to the coverage ratio reported to the board.
Any encumbered or matching-adjustment-assigned asset counted in the buffer is a fail.
testing.done: every buffer asset is proven unencumbered and unassigned, haircuts are evidenced, and the coverage ratio recomputes.

testing.step: Re-perform the collateral call projection against actual calls
actions: Take the 25 sampled settled margin calls and compare each to what the projection would have predicted for that day's market move.
Identify the largest single-day actual call in the year and compare it to the plan's projected largest call.
Confirm each sampled call was met from approved buffer assets in the eligible collateral form and within the settlement deadline.
Any call met by selling a non-buffer or matching adjustment asset is an exception and must be traced to its authorisation.
testing.done: actual calls are compared to projected calls, the largest actual call is benchmarked, and every sampled call was met from approved buffer assets.

testing.step: Test the contingency funding plan's actions are real
actions: Take each committed facility named in the plan and read the current agreement for amount, expiry, covenants and any material adverse change clause.
Confirm the amount and timing claimed in the plan match the agreement rather than an expired or uncommitted line.
Test the repo route by confirming active documentation with at least two counterparties and current eligibility of the assets named.
Confirm the named invocation authority is a current post-holder and that the escalation contact list is in date.
testing.done: every funding action in the plan is supported by a current agreement or documented counterparty route, with in-date invocation authorities.

testing.step: Test the monthly monitoring and breach escalation actually operated
actions: Confirm each of the twelve monthly dashboards was published by the fifth business day and record any that were late.
Take three months and re-perform the actual-versus-projected variance analysis, confirming every variance above 10% was explained.
Take every indicator breach in the year and confirm it was escalated to the Chief Risk Officer on the day observed, not in the monthly pack.
Confirm each breach appears in the GRC log with an owner and an action.
testing.done: all twelve dashboards are evidenced with timing, variance explanations re-perform, and every breach was escalated same-day and logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, quantified effect and owner
actions: Raise one record per exception naming the horizon or scenario affected and the shortfall in pounds where one exists.
Assign a root cause — liability bucketing, optimistic haircut, encumbered buffer asset, unrun scenario, stale facility, late escalation — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly stress run, not the next annual plan.
Where an exception reveals a projected shortfall at any horizon, open a Fundamental Rule 7 notification assessment with the Chief Risk Officer.
testing.done: every exception is quantified by horizon, root-caused, owned, dated before the next quarterly run, with notification assessed for shortfalls.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Risk Committee
actions: Compute the exception count against the no-projected-shortfall and buffer-monetisability thresholds.
State the conclusion — plan reliable / reliable with exceptions / not reliable — with workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside Treasury and Investments and set no haircut or scenario, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Risk Committee before the board approves the plan, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception count and has been reported to the Risk Committee before board approval of the plan.
